findings.title: Shipped and refund mails carry the personal order link without renewing its 7-day expiry, so the link is dead on arrival for any shipment or refund more than 7 days after payment
findings.evidence: Every order mail ends with the personal link: email.ts:371-372 'صفحة طلبك (الرابط شخصي، لا تشاركه):' then `${siteUrl}/orders#${number}.${token}`, the token derived from the order's current version (outbox.ts:177). The link lives while orders.access_token_expires_at > now(); it is set to now()+7 days only at payment (payment_core.sql:1143, 1151), order_resolve (order_operations.sql:967), paid_asset_set (delivery.sql:459) and recovery (delivery.sql:236, 242); contract section 4 (P08-CONTRACT.md:170) and operations.md:791 list exactly these. fulfillment_update queues `order_shipped` (order_operations.sql:720-724) and finance.refund_succeed queues `order_refunded` (final def stats_disputes.sql:213) without touching the expiry. order_access then answers NOT_FOUND for `access_token_expires_at <= now()` (delivery.sql:94) and OrderPage shows «لم نجد هذا الطلب، أو انتهت صلاحية رابطه.» with the recovery form.
findings.impact: A buyer whose book ships more than 7 days after payment (every preorder by design, most signed editions) gets a shipping mail whose order-page link fails, and every refund that follows a return (shipped, returned, received, refunded: always past day 7) mails a dead link too. The buyer must find the recovery form, type the address and wait for another mail (3 an hour per address, 20 order_link mails a day in all). Nothing detects it.
findings.proposed_fix: Where the two mails are queued, renew the link as paid_asset_set does: in fulfillment_update when cardinality(v_done) > 0 and p_state = 'shipped', and in finance.refund_succeed's attempt branch, `update finance.orders set access_token_expires_at = greatest(access_token_expires_at, now() + interval '7 days') where id = <order>`; add the rule to contract section 4.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack: pay an order with the emulator, then `update finance.orders set access_token_expires_at = now() - interval '1 minute' where order_number = '<N>'` (day 8), ship a line through fulfillment_update as staff, run the outbox, open the mailed /orders#<N>.<token>: the orders function answers 404 NOT_FOUND (wrong result).
findings.prior_overlap: Partly the round-05 'uncovered' item (a receipt or recovery link sent more than 7 days late because the quota held it); that names quota delays only, not mails queued after day 7 by design.

findings.title: The payment reconciliation job records every run, but no screen reads it: the owner home lists only four jobs
findings.evidence: AdminHome.tsx:33 `const KNOWN_JOBS = ['email_outbox', 'site_build', 'media_sweep', 'backup'] as const` and :372 renders `KNOWN_JOBS.map(...)` only; JOB_LABEL (:25-30) has no payments entry. jobs.ts:24-45 and payments.ts:749-765 write job_run_record('payments_reconcile', ok|partial|failed|skipped) on every run, and job_runs_latest returns that row, which the screen drops.
findings.impact: While payments are live the job is the safety net behind a missed webhook and a buyer who closed the return page: it settles paid invoices, cancels second invoices and settles in-flight refunds. If it stops (cron gone, a Vault value missing) or records skipped/failed every minute, no screen says so; orders_alerts' unverifiedAttempts only moves when the job runs, so a dead job also silences that count. A paid order can expire unnoticed until the buyer complains.
findings.proposed_fix: Add 'payments_reconcile' to KNOWN_JOBS and JOB_LABEL («مطابقة المدفوعات») with a stale rule while payment rows are due (the shape of outbox_due_since over the three next_check_at columns).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CONTRACT-01; artifacts/acceptance/P08/rounds/round-12b.md lines 23, 124, 196 (recorded as uncovered and documented with SQL, not fixed, not in PLANS/ISSUES.md)

findings.title: refund_settle's stale-read branch has no clock: a refund whose fetched total stays between its origin and its raised `before` is re-leased every minute for ever
findings.evidence: refunds.sql:600-611: when p_provider_refunded < v_before and >= v_origin the only action is `update finance.refunds r set next_check_at = now() + interval '1 minute'` ('A stale read decides nothing'). No check_count step and no created_at + 15 minutes rule (the not-landed branch has it at :619), and refund_checked's 24-hour rule runs only when the fetch itself fails. The comment at :562 says 'every fresh read ends the refund within 15 minutes of its creation'.
findings.impact: If Moyasar keeps answering a refunded total below the `before` this refund was moved to (a dashboard refund the ledger recorded and the provider later reversed, or a read that never catches up), the refund stays in flight for ever: every new refund of that payment and order_resolve answer REFUND_IN_FLIGHT, the job calls the provider every minute, and no owner alert is raised. Contract section 3 promises that no state waits for ever.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the branch the not-landed branch's clock: once now() >= created_at + 15 minutes, refund_fail(id, 'NOT_APPLIED') with one refund_unverified alert (or next_check_at null plus the alert); back off through check_count before that.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CONTRACT-02

findings.title: A refund of the other payment mode can never leave flight after the switch to live: refund_ref has no mode guard and «أعد الفحص» answers 'provider unreachable, try later' for ever
findings.evidence: refund_ref(p_actor, p_refund) (refunds.sql:797-823) reads the refund with no environment test, unlike payment_attempt_ref(.., p_mode) (payment_core.sql:1370, `and a.environment = p_mode`). refundRecheck (refunds.ts:264-271) fetches the payment with the live key, Moyasar answers 404, and the action answers unavailable(): 503 «تعذّر الوصول إلى بوابة الدفع الآن. لم يتغيّر شيء؛ حاول بعد قليل.». payment_reconcile_claim parks such a refund with next_check_at null and error 'MODE_CHANGED' but keeps status submitting/uncertain (payment_core.sql:1429-1434); refund-record-external answers NOT_FOUND for the test attempt. reconciliation_list lists in-flight refunds of both modes, ReconciliationView.tsx:375-396 offers the recheck with no «تجريبي» badge (refund_json has no environment), orders_alerts counts 'uncertain' refunds of both modes. payments-runbook.md:209 says such a refund 'stays for a person to settle at Moyasar' and operations.md:951-952 that 'A test row on a live site is labelled «تجريبي»'.
findings.impact: A sandbox refund still submitting or uncertain when PAYMENTS_MODE becomes live (E02) stays on the owner's reconciliation screen and in «تحتاج مطابقة» for ever; each recheck tells him the provider is unreachable and to try later, and settling it at Moyasar changes nothing in the ledger. Only SQL by hand clears it. No money is at risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Give refund_ref a p_mode and answer NOT_FOUND for a refund whose attempt or review payment is of another environment, and in the claim's MODE_CHANGED branch move such refunds out of flight (status 'failed', error 'MODE_CHANGED'); add the step to the runbook's 'Before live'.

findings.title: The checkout sends a phone the page no longer shows: a hidden invalid phone gets a field error the buyer cannot see, and a valid one is stored on a digital order

The phone input (:653) and its error span exist only inside `{quote.physical && (` (:648). checkout.ts:402-407 normalizes any non-empty phone and answers 422 INVALID with fieldErrors.phone; CheckoutForm.tsx:404-417 maps it to errors.phone, focuses #checkout-phone (not in the page) and returns without a submitError. checkout_create nulls only the address for a digital cart (checkout_payment.sql:527) and stores v_phone in the order and a new customers row.

findings.title: payments_kick gives the reconciliation run 15 s while one run may spend 60 s on provider calls and records itself only at the end
findings.evidence: payments_kick posts {job: 'payments_reconcile'} with `timeout_milliseconds := 15000` (payment_core.sql:1667-1672; comment :1666 '15 s: a cold function start can exceed pg_net's 5 s default'). runPaymentsReconcile keeps taking rows for RUN_BUDGET_MS = 60_000 (payments.ts:48), each provider call may take 10 s, the claim leases up to 10 attempts, 10 events and 5 refunds, and job_run_record is written after the loop (payments.ts:749).
findings.impact: If the 15 s bound is enforced and the edge runtime stops the request when pg_net drops it, a slow provider cuts every run short: the rows not reached wait out their 2-minute lease and the run is never recorded. If not, nothing is lost. The vendor pages disagree (doc_claims_checked), so only a run settles it.
findings.proposed_fix: Answer the kick at once and run the reconciliation inside EdgeRuntime.waitUntil(), or raise the kick's timeout above the run budget (75000); correct the comment's '5 s default'.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack, emulator delaying GET /invoices/:id by 12 s, six due attempts: let pg_cron fire payments_kick once, then `select status_code, error_msg from net._http_response order by created desc limit 1` (expect a timeout) and `select * from public.job_runs_latest() where job = 'payments_reconcile'` plus the attempts' next_check_at. Wrong result: no run row and the slow rows still leased and unprocessed.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CONTRACT-03

findings.title: A line can be shipped while an in-flight refund that fully refunds it is still unsettled; when it lands the buyer keeps both the goods and the money
findings.evidence: fulfillment_update only refuses lines that SUCCEEDED refunds have already fully refunded: lines 686-695 `and coalesce(finance.item_fully_refunded(f.order_item_id), false)` (item_fully_refunded, payment_core.sql:475-495, counts `r.status = 'succeeded'` only). It never reads refunds in 'submitting'/'uncertain', although their allocation is stored at refund_request time (refunds.sql:466-473). order_resolve has exactly this guard (order_operations.sql:955-960 REFUND_IN_FLIGHT, added by the orchestrator in round 7b for the same reason: 'that refund may still take a line this would commit'). fulfillment_update did not get it. The admin UI (OrderView.tsx:238-244, 688-689) also checks only fullyRefunded.
findings.impact: The owner refunds an unshipped book because the buyer cancelled. The provider call times out, so the refund stays 'uncertain' for up to 15 minutes (24 h+ while fetches fail). Operations sees the line still 'preparing' and not refunded, and ships it. The job then settles the refund as succeeded: the item has shipped, its stock is gone, and the buyer has the money back. Each occurrence loses one item's value. It needs two people acting within the uncertain window.
findings.proposed_fix: In fulfillment_update, for p_state in ('preparing','shipped'), after the order lock: refuse with REFUND_IN_FLIGHT (with itemIds) when a refund of the order's paying attempt in ('submitting','uncertain') allocates any of the moved items. Simpler: refuse when any refund of the order is in flight, mirroring order_resolve. Show the code in OrderView.
findings.proof_recipe: On a paid order with a physical line A (preparing): select refund_request(owner, order, attempt, null, <A cost>, 'x', '{"items":[{"itemId":"A","amount":<A cost>}],"shipping":0}', gen_random_uuid(), repeat('a',64), null, 0) -> state new (refund 'submitting'). As an operations JWT: select fulfillment_update(order, array[A], 'shipped', 'SMSA', '123', null). Expected today, which is the defect: {ok:true, changed:1}. Then refund_settle(refund, <A cost>) -> succeeded: item A is both shipped and fully refunded.
findings.prior_overlap: round-07b orchestrator fix added REFUND_IN_FLIGHT to order_resolve only

findings.title: The refund balance ignores recorded chargebacks: a payment the bank already reversed can be refunded again in full
findings.evidence: refund_request's balance check is `if v_confirmed::bigint + p_amount > v_captured then ... EXCEEDS_BALANCE` (line 442), with v_confirmed = succeeded refunds only (404-407). Nothing in refunds.sql reads finance.disputes. dispute_record (stats_disputes.sql:418-560) 'never creates a refund and never changes an attempt', so a recorded `chargeback`/`against_seller` row leaves the whole captured amount refundable. OrderView shows disputes in their own section, and the refund form does not mention them (RefundView.tsx contains no 'dispute').
findings.impact: A buyer opens a bank chargeback and also asks the shop for a refund. The owner records the chargeback from Moyasar's email (the money is already debited from the settlement). Then, the same day or later, he refunds the same payment from the admin, and the buyer is paid twice, up to the full order total. Moyasar documents no chargeback API, so nothing at the provider is known to refuse the refund.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner ruling, then a small change: while the target's latest dispute row of kind 'chargeback' is against_seller, refund_request either refuses (e.g. CHARGEBACK_RECORDED) or requires an explicit acknowledgement. At minimum, RefundView shows the attempt's chargeback rows above the amount fields.
findings.prior_overlap: none found in round-09/11b records

findings.title: An order access token can never be revoked, and anyone with a leaked link and the buyer's address can keep it alive indefinitely through recovery
findings.evidence: order_recover_apply with no hash: `update finance.orders o set access_token_expires_at = now() + interval '7 days' ... where o.id = r.order_id and o.access_token_version = r.version and o.access_token_expires_at > now()` (lines 234-238). It renews the SAME token whenever it is unexpired, before the mail cap and regardless of it (lines 248-258); orders-access.test.ts:487 confirms the link is renewed even when no mail is queued. In supabase/migrations, only order_recover_apply's expired branch (lines 240-243) and checkout write access_token_hash or access_token_version. No staff or buyer action rotates or revokes a link, in SQL or in the UI. PLANS/VERIFICATION.md 'Non-negotiable invariant tests': 'Tokens hash-stored/expiring/revocable'.
findings.impact: A buyer's order link leaks: a forwarded receipt, a shared screenshot, or a buyer posting it. Whoever has it reads the order and its tracking, files return requests and issues downloads of the paid PDF/EPUB (10 tokens x 3 links a day). Every recovery request for the buyer's address (Turnstile, 3 an hour) pushes the expiry 7 days further, so the 7-day expiry never takes effect. Neither the buyer nor the owner can kill the link; the most the owner can do is revoke the entitlement through a dispute row.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an owner/operations function `order_link_rotate(p_order)`, plus an admin action that derives the next version's hash in the function as recoveryItems does. It bumps access_token_version, stores the new hash and queues one order_link mail. Optionally, recovery stops renewing an unexpired token when the request did not come from that token's holder.
findings.prior_overlap: round-07 ruled that recovery must not kill a working link; revocation itself was never discussed

findings.title: Priority-0 order mail can use the whole Resend day, leaving no room for staff sign-in codes and holding later receipts until 03:00 Riyadh
findings.evidence: outbox_claim: `and v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - case o.priority when 0 then 0 when 1 then p_reserve else p_reserve + p_low_reserve end` with p_daily_quota = DAILY_QUOTA = 100 (outbox.ts:41). Priority 0 covers receipts, order_shipped, order_refunded, order_ready (one per waiting entitlement, no cap; paid_asset_set delivery.sql:447-466) and owner_alert (one row per active owner), and all of it can go up to 100. v_sent_today counts outbox rows only, while Supabase Auth's codes use the same Resend account over SMTP (I28). outbox.ts:47-53 says the reserve 'keeps the last sends of the Resend daily limit free for them', which stops being true once priority 0 passes 80; ARCHITECTURE.md:113 says the same. Resend: 100/day on Free, the same limits over SMTP as over the API, no daily quota on paid plans.
findings.impact: On a launch day with roughly 80-100 priority-0 sends (receipts, owner alerts and shipping mails, or one file upload for many waiting preorders), Resend answers 429 for the rest of the UTC day. Buyers who pay later get no receipt or order link until 00:00 UTC (03:00 Riyadh), and an owner or operations member whose session has lapsed cannot get a sign-in code to reach the admin.
findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision first: either a Resend plan without a daily quota before launch (then raise DAILY_QUOTA), or a small code floor that priority 0 cannot cross (priority 0 stops at p_daily_quota - p_code_reserve). Either way, correct the outbox.ts:47-53 comment and ARCHITECTURE.md:113.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-01; AUDIT-1 S04.1 (the reserve for codes), which contract section 13 item 5 later bypassed by widening priority 0

findings.title: A paid buyer whose address was mistyped or suppressed never receives the order link, and staff cannot correct the address or reissue it
findings.evidence: The link reaches a buyer only by mail to orders.customer_email. The receipt comes from order_try_commit (payment_core.sql:714-716). Recovery matches `o.email_hash = finance.recipient_hash(v_email)` (delivery.sql:192) and mails the address stored on the order row (252-254). In supabase/migrations nothing updates customer_email or email_hash after checkout, and nothing deletes from finance.email_suppressions. order_detail exposes no token or idempotency key, by design. CheckoutForm.tsx:612-628 has one email field and no confirmation field. docs/operations.md 'A lost link' (797-803) offers only the recovery form.
findings.impact: A buyer who types name@gmial.com pays and sees the order once on the return page. After that they get no receipt, no link and no paid file. Recovery with the correct address finds nothing because it hashes to a different value. The owner can see the order and the phone number but has no action that delivers the link. If the typo is someone else's real address, that stranger receives the order link and can download the book. A hard bounce leads to the same dead end, because the address is then suppressed for every later mail.
findings.proposed_fix: An owner action (fresh TOTP), order_contact_set(p_order, p_email). Under the order lock it rewrites customer_email and email_hash, bumps access_token_version with a new hash derived in the function (so the link sent to the wrong address dies), writes an audit row without the address and queues one order_link. Also document a recipe for lifting a suppression.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-03

findings.title: refund_settle's stale-read branch has no time limit: a provider total stuck between origin and before keeps a refund in flight indefinitely, fetched every minute, with no alert
findings.evidence: Lines 600-611: a total below `before` but not below provider_refunded_origin runs `update finance.refunds r set next_check_at = now() + interval '1 minute'` and nothing else. There is no check_count, no 15-minute rule (619-630) and no 24-hour rule (refund_checked runs only on failed fetches). Only the in-between branch (613-617) raises `before`, and only to a total the provider itself reported, so a later total that stays below it is a real decrease that the code does not treat as one. The header (refunds.sql:12-14) and contract section 3 ('there is no state that waits for ever') promise that every in-flight refund ends within 15 minutes once the provider answers.
findings.impact: If the provider ever lowers its refunded total after a dashboard refund was recorded (for example a dashboard refund that later fails at the bank), the in-flight refund never ends. Every refund, external recording and order_resolve on that payment answers REFUND_IN_FLIGHT. payments_kick wakes the job every minute, the provider is fetched every minute indefinitely, and no owner alert is ever raised.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply the same clock in the stale branch: once now() >= created_at + 15 minutes, treat a total still below `before` as PROVIDER_TOTAL_DECREASED (refund_fail plus the refund_total_decreased alert). Before that point, back off as the unchanged branch does.
findings.proof_recipe: Request refund R (amount 500) at provider total 300 (origin 300). refund_settle(R, 450) takes the in-between branch and sets before = 450. Move R.created_at back 2 hours, then call refund_settle(R, 300) twice. Expected today, which is the defect: status stays 'submitting', next_check_at = now() + 1 minute each time, check_count unchanged, and no owner_alert row in finance.email_outbox.
findings.prior_overlap: the R6-A3 fix introduced the branch

findings.title: A refund parked MODE_CHANGED can never be settled or closed, and it blocks every later refund of that payment
findings.evidence: payment_reconcile_claim runs `update finance.refunds r set next_check_at = null, error = 'MODE_CHANGED' ... where r.status in ('submitting', 'uncertain')` (1429-1434), which leaves the refund in flight. The only exits are refund_result (only from the call that created the refund) and refund_settle, which needs a successful fetch. refund_ref has no mode, and refunds.ts:269-270 answers 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE when the other mode's payment answers 404 to the configured key. refund_request and refund_record_external answer REFUND_IN_FLIGHT (refunds.sql:421-423, 748-750), and so does order_resolve (order_operations.sql:955-960). The contract says such a refund 'stays in flight for a person to settle at the provider', but no function lets a person close the ledger row.
findings.impact: A sandbox refund that is in flight when PAYMENTS_MODE switches to live (the E02 cut-over) stays on the owner's reconciliation screen permanently, and its recheck always says the provider is unreachable. Its order can never be resolved or refunded again. Live money is affected only if the site is switched back to test while a live refund is in flight, and then a recheck under the live key resolves it.
findings.proposed_fix: Either have the claim fail other-mode refunds outright (status failed, error MODE_CHANGED, one owner alert), or give the owner a step-up action that closes a MODE_CHANGED refund as failed with an audit row.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-05; open risk listed by the round-06 worker

findings.title: The owner's «تحتاج مطابقة» count leaves out rows that need a person: refunds stuck in submitting and paid attempts the provider voided
findings.evidence: orders_alerts counts `'uncertainRefunds', (select count(*) from finance.refunds r where r.status = 'uncertain')` (order_operations.sql:493) and has no count for a provider status. reconciliation_list, by contrast, lists refunds `where r.status in ('submitting', 'uncertain')` (587) and paid attempts with the PROVIDER_STATUS reason (556-558: provider_status not in ('paid','refunded') and confirmed refunds below captured). A refund stays submitting when the admin function dies between refund_request and refund_result (refunds.ts:250-255), and refund_checked changes only the schedule, never the status (refunds.sql:662-664). If a void leaves the payment's refunded total unchanged (undocumented; sandbox item 11, which is why refund_record_external handles voided specially), externalRefunds does not count it either. admin-orders.ts:232-246 describes the count as the sum of what the reconciliation screen lists.
findings.impact: A voided payment (money returned to the buyer) leaves its order 'paid' with lines to ship. The home shows «للشحن» but «تحتاج مطابقة» 0, so if the single provider_status alert mail is missed, operations can ship goods nobody paid for. Separately, a refund whose result was never written and whose payment cannot be fetched stays in flight for 24 hours (then one mail) and after that indefinitely, blocking refunds of that payment, and none of this is counted.
findings.proposed_fix: Count in orders_alerts what the reconciliation screen lists as needing a person: refunds in ('submitting','uncertain') (or submitting ones older than a few minutes) and paid attempts with the PROVIDER_STATUS reason. Consider refusing fulfillment_update while the paying attempt's provider_status is voided.
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: A full refund of a preorder line that has already shipped releases its reservation, so capacity for a copy that has left the shelf can be sold again
findings.evidence: refund_succeed (the version that runs) does `update finance.inventory_reservations x set state = 'released', released_at = now() where x.order_id = v_order.id and x.preorder and x.state <> 'released' and x.variant_id in (select i.variant_id ... where coalesce(finance.item_fully_refunded(i.id), false))` (200-206), with no condition on finance.fulfillments.state. finance.preorder_committed (payment_core.sql:440-449) counts only committed preorder reservations against preorder_capacity. By contrast, a refund never restores ordinary stock (refunds.sql:197-198), and return_receive adds nothing for a preorder line (order_operations.sql:902).
findings.impact: Refunding a shipped preorder copy as goodwill (the buyer keeps it) frees one unit of capacity. One more preorder can then be sold than there are copies, and that buyer later ends up in paid_needs_resolution or waits for a copy that does not exist. Preorder is off at opening (Anas, Q05), so this stays latent until the owner turns it on.
findings.proposed_fix: Release a preorder reservation on refund only for lines that have not shipped: add `and not exists (select 1 from finance.fulfillments f join finance.order_items i2 on i2.id = f.order_item_id where i2.order_id = x.order_id and i2.variant_id = x.variant_id and f.state in ('shipped','delivered'))`.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-02

findings.title: A carrier or tracking value mistyped at shipping can never be corrected; the buyer is mailed and shown the wrong number
findings.evidence: fulfillment_update: `when 'shipped' then f.state = 'preparing' or (f.state = 'shipped' and f.carrier is not distinct from v_carrier and f.tracking is not distinct from v_tracking)` (677-679). Any other carrier or tracking value on a shipped line is BAD_TRANSITION (682-684), and the `delivered` branch never writes them (726-733). No other function writes finance.fulfillments.carrier or tracking. The order_shipped mail (order_email_data shipment, order_emails.sql:112-127) and order_access (delivery.sql:124-126) show the stored values.
findings.impact: A tracking number with one wrong digit stays on the buyer's order page and in the shipping mail for the life of the order. Staff can only correct it by telling the buyer over the phone.
findings.proposed_fix: Allow shipped -> shipped with a new carrier/tracking as an audited correction (with a version bump), and queue one more order_shipped mail keyed on the new values (e.g. dedupe `order_shipped:<orderId>:<md5(items)>:<md5(carrier|tracking)>`).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-04

findings.title: A receipt sent after the order was refunded tells the buyer the payment is being reviewed
findings.evidence: renderReceipt: `if (order.status !== 'paid') { ... 'وصلتنا دفعتك للطلب رقم ${number} بمبلغ ${money(total)}، ونراجع الطلب الآن.' }` (403-410) uses one sentence for both paid_needs_resolution and refunded. order_email_data reads the live status at send time (order_emails.sql:57). A receipt can wait behind the quota (priority 0 stops only at 100) or an outage while the owner fully refunds a paid_needs_resolution order.
findings.impact: The buyer first reads «ونراجع الطلب الآن» about an order that has already been refunded, then gets the refund mail. That is a confusing pair of messages on a money journey the design wants calm and official.
findings.proposed_fix: Handle `refunded` separately in renderReceipt: either one line saying the payment arrived and was refunded, with the refunded total, or close the row with a state code that outbox_attention leaves out, as it does NO_FILE.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-06

findings.title: The refund step-up lives only in the admin Edge Function; the SQL rechecks the owner role and the Data API cannot reach it
findings.evidence: handleAdmin: `if (!staff.recentTotp) return fail(403, 'STEP_UP_REQUIRED', ...)` for refund-create (223-226) and refund-record-external (230-233). recentTotp = hasRecentTotp(claims) (aal2 plus a totp amr entry within 300 s, recent-totp.ts:8-19), with claims from auth.getClaims (staff.ts:36-48). refund_request, refund_record_external and refund_ref only recheck that p_actor is an active owner (refunds.sql:344-348, 701-705, 808-812); they are revoked from public/anon/authenticated and granted to service_role (827-839). By contract, refund-recheck and paid-file-complete need no step-up because they move no money.
findings.impact: None as built: an operations member or an owner with a stale aal2 session cannot reach the refund SQL directly, and the function refuses them (403 FORBIDDEN / STEP_UP_REQUIRED). The guarantee depends on this one function, so any future route that calls refund_request as service_role must repeat the check.
findings.proposed_fix: None required. Optionally pass the verified aal and amr time to the SQL and assert them there, so the rule sits next to the money.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-POST-07

findings.title: Refund amount boundaries hold in the ledger; the provider's minimum is undocumented, and a refusal ends cleanly as failed
findings.evidence: `p_amount is null or p_amount < 1` raises 22023 (349-355), and 1 halala is reserved. `v_confirmed::bigint + p_amount > v_captured` is EXCEEDS_BALANCE (442-444), so exactly the remainder passes and refund_succeed marks the order refunded. In refunds.ts, `halalas = z.number().int().positive().max(INT_MAX)` (46) gives 0 a 422 before the SQL runs. The allocation must sum to the amount (refund_allocation_ok 182), and each item stays within its line cost. A provider 4xx becomes refund_fail REFUND_REFUSED (refunds.ts:180-182, refunds.sql:534-535), which frees the balance. docs.moyasar.com/api/payments/05-refund-payment documents no minimum.
findings.impact: None in the ledger. Moyasar may refuse a 1-halala refund (unknown until the sandbox, E02 item 8); that would only show as a failed refund.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the sandbox answer for a tiny refund in the runbook. If a minimum exists, refuse amounts below it in refund_request with its own code and Arabic sentence.
findings.proof_recipe: Sandbox (E02): refund 1 halala of a paid test payment through refund-create; record the HTTP status and the payment's refunded total.

findings.title: Parking other-mode work expires still-payable live invoices with no alert and no screen; a payment on them is never recorded
findings.evidence: payment_reconcile_claim first runs `update finance.payment_attempts a set next_check_at = null, last_error = 'MODE_CHANGED', ... status = case when a.status in ('creating','pending','uncertain') then 'expired' ...` for every due attempt whose environment is not p_mode (lines 1424-1428). No owner_alert is queued there. reconciliation_list (order_operations.sql:553-561) flags only UNCERTAIN, UNVERIFIED, PROVIDER_STATUS and EXTERNAL_REFUND, and orders_alerts counts `last_error = 'UNVERIFIED'` only (493-496), never MODE_CHANGED. The webhook closes an other-mode event with the final outcome 'mode_mismatch' (payments.ts:461, 637), which event_needs_person (order_operations.sql:179) does not count. payment_view filters on `o.environment = p_mode`, so the buyer's return page answers 'unknown'. A parked attempt has next_check_at null and is not UNVERIFIED, so finance.order_erasable (stats_disputes.sql:52-66) lets the 90-day purge, or a buyer's erase at once, delete the attempt, which is the only row that maps the Moyasar invoice to the order. tests/integration/payment.test.ts:2213-2214 pins the result: the live attempt is expired / next_check_at null / MODE_CHANGED and `(await claim('live')).attempts` is empty. Switching back to live never re-checks it.
findings.impact: Precondition: PAYMENTS_MODE is switched (live to test, for a sandbox run or a rollback after launch) while live invoices are still open. A buyer who pays such an invoice is charged real money. The webhook is closed as mode_mismatch, the job never asks again, the order stays expired, the return page says the order is unknown, no owner alert is sent and nothing shows on the reconciliation screen. Switching back to live does not recover it, because the attempt has no due time and the event is closed. Only a buyer who reloads the return page within 24 hours of the invoice's expiry triggers a late settle. Otherwise the payment is lost from the ledger and the evidence is purged after 90 days. This breaks contract invariant 11 ('anomalous money is never lost').
findings.proposed_fix: In payment_reconcile_claim, when a parked attempt has a provider_invoice_id and was active (or its invoice expired less than 24 hours ago), queue `finance.owner_alert('attempt_mode_changed', a.id::text, jsonb_build_object('attemptId', a.id, 'orderId', a.order_id))` for each such row. Alternatively, mark it last_error = 'UNVERIFIED' so the existing screen, alert path and purge exclusion apply. Add MODE_CHANGED to reconciliation_list's reasons. Say in the runbook that PAYMENTS_MODE must not change while attempts of the current mode are active or due.
findings.proof_recipe: As postgres on a local stack: insert a live order (environment 'live', status 'pending_payment') and an attempt (environment 'live', status 'pending', provider_invoice_id '<uuid>', next_check_at now() - interval '1 minute'). Run `select public.payment_reconcile_claim('test');`, then `select status, last_error, next_check_at from finance.payment_attempts where id = <attempt>`. Expected wrong result: expired / MODE_CHANGED / null. `select count(*) from finance.email_outbox where kind = 'owner_alert' and created_at > now() - interval '1 minute'` returns 0. With request.jwt claims for an owner, `select public.reconciliation_list()` does not list the attempt. After `update finance.orders set status = 'expired'`, `select finance.order_erasable(o) from finance.orders o where id = <order>` returns true.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-PAY-02 (same defect, confirmed independently). R2-06 (round 2) introduced this parking to stop other-mode rows being due for ever. That fix holds, but it parks silently. Not in ISSUES I28-I51.

findings.title: A preorder hold paid after the owner switches the preorder off can only end paid_needs_resolution, and order_resolve can never commit it
findings.evidence: order_try_commit decides a line by the reservation's snapshot flag: `if r.res_preorder then v_free := coalesce(r.preorder_capacity, 0) - finance.preorder_committed(r.variant_id) - case when v_own then 0 else finance.active_holds(r.variant_id) end;` (648-650). The variant form clears the capacity when preorder is switched off: `preorder_capacity: preorder ? (values.preorder_capacity ?? null) : null` (src/admin/tables/variants.ts:97). So v_free <= 0 for every reservation made while the variant was a preorder. order_resolve calls the same function (order_operations.sql:963) and answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE for ever. tests/integration/payment.test.ts:1664-1672 pins the paid_needs_resolution outcome with 5 units in stock. docs/operations.md 'Preorders' (1083-1089) tells the owner to switch the preorder off when the copies arrive and says nothing about holds that are still open.
findings.impact: Precondition: a preorder variant is switched off (the copies arrived, as the operations guide instructs) while a buyer holds an unpaid preorder reservation, or while a late payment on such an order can still land. The buyer is charged and gets the 'under review' receipt. The owner cannot deliver through «إكمال الطلب» even with copies on the shelf. The only exits are a refund, or switching the variant back to a public preorder with a capacity and a future date. Preorder is off at opening (Anas, Q05), so this bites only once the capability is used.
findings.proposed_fix: In order_try_commit, use the capacity rule only while the variant is still a preorder (`r.res_preorder and v.preorder`). Otherwise judge the line by the stock rule (own hold: stock >= quantity; else stock - active_holds) and include it in the stock decrement loop (`not (coalesce(x.preorder,false) and v.preorder)`). Add one SQL test: preorder hold, switch off with stock, pay, expect paid with stock decremented.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-PAY-01 (confirmed). The lead's alternative (keep the capacity on switch-off) covers a line whose own hold is still valid. A reacquired line would then compare the old capacity against active_holds that now include ordinary stock holds. Deciding by the stock rule once the variant is no longer a preorder avoids both problems.

findings.title: A payment that is already fully refunded when first fetched settles the order as paid: files granted, receipt sent, stock taken
findings.evidence: `v_charged := v_status in ('paid', 'refunded');` (1002). Nothing in steps 5-7 looks at v_refunded, so a first-seen payment with status 'refunded' and refunded = amount reaches step 8. There, finance.order_try_commit grants entitlements, creates fulfilments, decrements stock and queues the receipt, and the order becomes 'paid' (1140-1145). Only then does `perform finance.attempt_provider_alerts(v_attempt.id, v_status)` (1180) raise external_refund. tests/integration/payment.test.ts:1361 pins `apply(started, { status: 'refunded', refunded: total })` with outcome 'paid'.
findings.impact: Precondition: the payment is refunded at Moyasar (the dashboard) before any of the four paths first settles it, for example after a webhook outage. The buyer gets the paid receipt and a working download for money already returned, and a physical line is queued for shipping, until the owner acts on the external_refund alert. Contract invariant 11 says anomalous money is never fulfilled. Here it is fulfilled for as long as the owner takes to react.
findings.proposed_fix: In step 8, when `v_refunded >= v_amount`, take the paid_needs_resolution branch instead of committing. The attempt is recorded paid, nothing is granted, shipped or decremented, and the existing needs_resolution alert asks the owner to record the refund.

findings.title: order_resolve delivers a paid_needs_resolution order whose payment was already refunded or voided at Moyasar
findings.evidence: order_resolve locks the order and the paying attempt. It refuses only `status <> 'paid_needs_resolution'` and a ledger refund in flight (`r.status in ('submitting','uncertain')`, 955-961), then calls `finance.order_try_commit(p_order, 'receipt:' || p_order::text || ':resolved')` (963) and sets the order paid. It never reads the attempt's provider_status or provider_refunded_halalas. apply_verified_payment keeps both current (payment_core.sql:1057-1063), and reconciliation_list already flags them as PROVIDER_STATUS / EXTERNAL_REFUND (order_operations.sql:556-560). The admin shows «إكمال الطلب» for every paid_needs_resolution order with no such condition (src/components/admin/OrderView.tsx:911-931).
findings.impact: Precondition: the buyer of a stuck order is refunded from Moyasar's dashboard (or the bank voids the payment), and the owner or a second owner then presses «إكمال الطلب» before recording the external refund. Stock is taken, files are granted, a shipment is queued and a second receipt is mailed for money that has gone back. The external_refund / provider_status alert exists, so this is an operator slip the function could refuse, not a silent loss.
findings.proposed_fix: In order_resolve, after locking the paying attempt, answer `{ok:false, code:'PROVIDER_CHANGED'}` when `a.provider_status not in ('paid','refunded')` or `a.provider_refunded_halalas > finance.attempt_refunds_known(a.id)`. Map the code to a sentence in OrderView.

findings.title: The invoice callback's 60-per-hour throttle is keyed on the caller's IP, and the only real caller is Moyasar's server
findings.evidence: payment_callback_begin: `if not finance.rate_limit_take('payment-callback:ip', p_ip_hash, 60, interval '1 hour') then return '{}'::jsonb;` (1343-1345). The hash comes from clientKeyHash(request) in payments.ts:485, which uses the connecting address (cf-connecting-ip). Moyasar's guide describes callback_url as 'An endpoint on your server, for receiving notifications about paid invoices' (https://docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/invoices/creating-invoices.md). That is a server-to-server POST, so every buyer's callback arrives from Moyasar's own egress addresses and spends a shared bucket.
findings.impact: Once more than 60 invoices are paid within an hour through one Moyasar egress address (a book launch; how many addresses Moyasar sends from is undocumented), every later callback from that address is answered {} and silently does nothing. No money is lost: the webhook, the return page and the job still settle. But the fast path the contract counts on disappears exactly when traffic peaks. A buyer who closed the return page waits for the webhook or for the job's 1-2-4-8 minute backoff. If the webhook is also late or misregistered, settlement of those orders slips to the job's schedule.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep a per-IP bucket only as a flood guard, with a limit far above any sales hour (for example 3600 an hour). Put the real limit on the invoice: after the id maps to an attempt worth asking, take `rate_limit_take('payment-callback:invoice', encode(sha256(convert_to(p_invoice_id,'UTF8')),'hex'), 10, interval '1 hour')`. Moyasar's one call per paid invoice then never shares a bucket with other buyers' invoices, and an abuser still gets no more than the 5-second fetched_at rule allows per attempt.
findings.prior_overlap: None found in rounds 02-04b, AUDIT-1, AUDIT-2 or ISSUES.

findings.title: order_resolve commits a coupon past its usage limit without the couponOverLimit mark apply_verified_payment writes
findings.evidence: order_resolve calls finance.order_try_commit (963), which commits the coupon 'whatever its limit' (payment_core.sql:691-697). It then audits only `jsonb_build_object('orderNumber', v_order.order_number, 'amount', v_order.total_halalas)` (969-971). The over-limit check exists only in apply_verified_payment (payment_core.sql:1168-1177), and only for its own 'paid' outcome. A paid_needs_resolution order commits nothing at payment time, so order_resolve commits its coupon later with no mark.
findings.impact: A coupon limited to N uses ends with N+1 committed redemptions when a paid_needs_resolution order is resolved after another order took the last use, and no audit row says so. An owner who reads the audit trail for over-limit commits (the contract's stated control) misses every case that goes through «إكمال الطلب».
findings.proposed_fix: In order_resolve, after the commit, compute the same `v_over` as apply (coupon_id not null, usage_limit not null and finance.coupon_uses(coupon) > usage_limit) and add `couponOverLimit: true` to the order.resolved summary.

Any invoice the store did not create through payment_attempt_begin is recorded as a review payment UNMAPPED_INVOICE with an owner alert (1007-1029), and the single webhook endpoint receives every payment of the Moyasar account. The runbook also does not say the Moyasar account must serve this store only: an invoice or payment link made in the dashboard, for a consulting session for instance, also lands in review with an alert.

plan_gaps.title: Nothing re-reads a paid attempt on a schedule: a dashboard refund or void whose webhook was dropped never reaches the ledger or the owner
plan_gaps.why_needed: apply_verified_payment sets next_check_at = null on a paid attempt (payment_core.sql 1162-1166), and payment_reconcile_claim leases only due rows (1437-1443). After settlement, the ledger learns of a refund or void made at Moyasar only from its webhook or from the owner's «أعد الفحص». Moyasar drops a webhook after six failed deliveries over about 3 h 41 min (webhook reference). The handler stores nothing and raises nothing for a wrong secret_token (payments.ts:434-435), so a mis-set MOYASAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET or a few hours of downtime is invisible. Payments still settle through the callback, the return page and the job, but the external_refund and provider_status alerts the runbook promises ('a webhook or a check raises the owner alert', payments-runbook.md:254) never fire. The order keeps its files and the statistics count money that went back.

findings.title: A dispute's «إيقاف الشحن» (fulfillment_stopped) stops nothing: the line stays in the to-ship list, fulfillment_update ships it, and operations never see the decision
findings.evidence: dispute_record with decision fulfillment_stopped only checks that the named items are `preparing` and inserts the row (stats_disputes.sql:522-531, 533-541). fulfillment_update (order_operations.sql:628-753) never reads finance.disputes: its refusals are ORDER_NOT_PAID, INVALID_ITEMS, BAD_TRANSITION, ITEM_REFUNDED and DEDICATION_NOT_DONE. The to_ship filter (243-247), orders_alerts.toShip (486-492) and order_lines_to_ship (53-63) ignore disputes; order_detail adds `disputes` only `if v_role = 'owner'` (415); OrderView.tsx:689 makes a line choosable unless it is fully refunded. DisputeForm offers «إيقاف الشحن» with line checkboxes and no hint that it is recorded only (DisputeForm.tsx:194-231). Contract section 6 (P08-CONTRACT.md:378) and the runbooks say 'only recorded'.
findings.impact: After a chargeback on a line still being prepared (a preorder waits for weeks), the owner records «إيقاف الشحن» and believes shipping is stopped; the line is still under «للشحن» for the operations member, who sees no dispute at all and ships it. The bank has taken the money back and the book is gone too.
findings.proposed_fix: In fulfillment_update refuse (a new code, e.g. SHIPPING_STOPPED with itemIds) an item named by a fulfillment_stopped row of a reference whose latest row has not lifted it, leave such lines out of the to_ship filter and count, and give operations a per-line flag in order_detail; amend contract section 6.
findings.proof_recipe: A paid order with one physical line in 'preparing': as the owner, dispute_record(<owner>, 'chargeback', 'CB-1', 0, <attempt>, null, <amount>, 'against_seller', current_date, 'test', null, 'fulfillment_stopped', array[<item>], 'test') -> ok. As operations: orders_list('to_ship', null, null, 50) still lists the order; order_detail(<order>) has no disputes key; fulfillment_update(<order>, array[<item>], 'shipped', 'SMSA', 'T1', null) -> {ok:true, changed:1} (wrong: expected a refusal).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-OPS-01 (rated high there); contract section 6 says the decision is only recorded

An uncertain creation whose invoice listing keeps failing is checked with `checkAttempt(deps, attempt.attemptId, 'job', false, null, 'INVOICE_LIST_FAILED')` (payments.ts:605-609); 24 hours after its invoice_expires_at the terminal rule makes it `expired`, `last_error = 'UNVERIFIED'`, next_check_at null (order_operations.sql:1124-1130), with provider_invoice_id still null. For that attempt neither branch runs, so payment_attempt_checked(prompt, ok), the only thing that clears the mark (order_operations.sql:1095-1100), is never called, and the job never claims it again. The round 7b test proves the clearing only by calling payment_attempt_checked in SQL on an attempt that has an invoice (order-operations.test.ts:1402-1416).

With the emulator up, call the admin action payment-recheck for it as the owner: reply {status:'expired'}; select last_error -> still 'UNVERIFIED' and orders_alerts().unverifiedAttempts unchanged (wrong: a person can never clear it).

findings.title: A confirmation the hourly backlog queues late gets a link that dies early: the purge's 7 days run from the last request, the link's 7 days from the queued mail
findings.evidence: notify_confirm_queue stamps only `set confirm_sent_at = now()` (line 124; updated_at is not touched and public.notifications has no trigger). The backlog picks pending rows with confirm_sent_at null `order by n.updated_at, n.id` (line 150), oldest first. The purge deletes `(n.status = 'pending' and n.updated_at < now() - interval '7 days')` (line 423), while notify.ts:174 honours a confirm link for 7 days after confirmSentAt. A row that waited d days behind the caps is mailed at day d and deleted at day 7 to 8, so its link lives 7-d days; a row that waited ~6.9 days gets a mail whose link 404s («الرابط غير صالح أو انتهت صلاحيته.») within hours, and the purge also deletes the unsent mail.
findings.impact: Precondition: the day's 30 confirmations (or the one-per-address-per-day cap for a visitor who signed up for several variants) held a sign-up back for days. The visitor who was told «sent» receives a confirmation that expires early or never arrives, so he is never told the item is back; the backlog spends the day's scarce budget on the rows least likely to be confirmed first.
findings.proposed_fix: Purge a pending row by its later clock: `n.status = 'pending' and greatest(n.updated_at, coalesce(n.confirm_sent_at, n.updated_at)) < now() - interval '7 days'` (or have notify_confirm_queue also set updated_at = now()).
findings.proof_recipe: In one rolled-back transaction with the day's buckets free: insert into public.notifications (email, variant_id, status, updated_at) values ('late@example.com', '<published out-of-stock variant>', 'pending', now() - interval '6 days 23 hours') returning id; select finance.notify_confirm_queue('<id>'); (what the backlog does for that row) -> 'queued', confirm_sent_at = now(), one notify_confirm outbox row. Then update public.notifications set updated_at = now() - interval '7 days 1 minute' where id = '<id>' (the purge's clock two hours later; confirm_sent_at untouched); select finance.notifications_purge(); Wrong result: the row and its unsent mail are deleted although its link was queued minutes ago and notify.ts:174 honours it for 7 days.
findings.prior_overlap: R8-06 (the backlog was the fix; this is its clock mismatch, not recorded)

findings.title: A sign-up that queues behind the purge's lock on an orphan availability row goes on without the row: the subscriber is stored but the sweep can never see him
findings.evidence: notify_subscribe runs `insert into finance.variant_availability (variant_id) values (p_variant) on conflict (variant_id) do nothing;` (204) then `perform 1 from finance.variant_availability a where a.variant_id = p_variant for update;` (205) and never checks FOUND. notifications_purge locks orphan rows (`for update skip locked`, 438) and deletes them in the next statement (439-441). When the sign-up's insert runs after the purge's lock but before its delete, the conflict is with a live row (a FOR UPDATE lock does not make the insert wait), so nothing is inserted; the FOR UPDATE then waits, and once the purge commits the deleted row is skipped (READ COMMITTED), the perform finds nothing, and the function inserts the notification and queues its confirmation with no availability row. The sweep iterates only finance.variant_availability rows, and no other path recreates the row except a later sign-up while the variant is out of stock. The header's claim that the purge's delete 'sees what a sign-up committed meanwhile' does not hold here: the sign-up is blocked and has committed nothing. Round 8's second audit ran only the other interleaving (purge already deleted, the insert waits and creates a new row).
findings.impact: Precondition: a sign-up for a variant whose last subscription the daily purge (03:37 GMT) is removing, inside the purge's lock-to-commit window (milliseconds, once a day). The visitor confirms and is never told when the item is back; he misses at least the next restock, until some other visitor signs up while the variant is out of stock.
findings.proposed_fix: In notify_subscribe, after the `for update`, when no row was found (`if not found`) insert the availability row again (`on conflict do nothing`) and lock it, repeating until a row is held; then the stale-true reset and the subscription go on as now.
findings.proof_recipe: Two sessions on a published, enabled variant V at stock 0 with an availability row and no notification. Session A: begin; select a.variant_id from finance.variant_availability a where a.variant_id = 'V' and not exists (select 1 from public.notifications n where n.variant_id = a.variant_id) for update skip locked; (the purge's statement, lines 434-438). Session B: select public.notify_subscribe(repeat('a',64), 'race@example.com', 'V', null); -> blocks. Session A: delete from finance.variant_availability a where a.variant_id = 'V' and not exists (select 1 from public.notifications n where n.variant_id = a.variant_id); commit; Session B answers {ok:true}. Wrong result: select count(*) from finance.variant_availability where variant_id = 'V' -> 0 while public.notifications holds the pending row; after notify_confirm and a restock, select finance.availability_sweep() -> 0 and no availability mail is queued for that subscriber.
findings.prior_overlap: R8-04 (its fix; the second audit ran only the delete-first interleaving)

findings.title: Switching a variant off preorder nulls its capacity, so a preorder line still on hold or waiting for resolution can never be committed: order_resolve answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE for ever and tells the owner to fix the stock
findings.evidence: The variant form writes `preorder_capacity: preorder ? (values.preorder_capacity ?? null) : null` (variants.ts:97), so «طلب مسبق» switched off stores capacity null (the table check only requires it while preorder is on). A reservation keeps the preorder flag it was created with (checkout_payment.sql:607-609), and finance.order_try_commit decides by that flag: `v_free := coalesce(r.preorder_capacity, 0) - finance.preorder_committed(r.variant_id) - ...` (payment_core.sql:649), which is <= 0 once capacity is null, so the line fails whatever the stock. apply_verified_payment then makes the order paid_needs_resolution, and order_resolve (order_operations.sql:962) goes through the same order_try_commit and returns STOCK_UNAVAILABLE on every try; the screen says «المخزون لا يكفي لعنصر في هذا الطلب؛ عدّل المخزون أو أعد مبلغ العنصر أولًا.» (admin-orders.ts:619), but no stock value helps. docs/operations.md («Net confirmed preorders out of real stock») tells the owner to switch preorder off when the copies arrive and says nothing about open holds.
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner switches a variant off preorder (the documented step when copies arrive, or a digital preorder whose file arrived) while a buyer's preorder hold is open (20 minutes) or a paid_needs_resolution order has a preorder line. The buyer has paid and cannot be delivered; the only ways out are a refund (a lost sale) or switching the variant back to a public preorder with a future date and a capacity, resolving, and switching it off again, which nothing tells the owner.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the capacity whatever the switch (variants.ts:97: `preorder_capacity: values.preorder_capacity ?? null`; nothing reads it while preorder is false: finance.availability, variant_public_state and checkout_price use stock then), so a held or waiting preorder line still commits against it; add one line to docs/operations.md's switch-off paragraph.
findings.proof_recipe: On the local stack: make a physical variant a preorder (capacity 5, a future date, a note); create an order for 1 unit and its invoice on the emulator; before paying, save the variant with «طلب مسبق» off and stock 10 through the admin form (or update public.product_variants set preorder = false, preorder_capacity = null, preorder_ships_on = null, preorder_note = null, stock = 10). Pay the invoice: the order becomes paid_needs_resolution. select public.order_resolve('<order id>') as the owner -> {ok:false, code:'STOCK_UNAVAILABLE'} although stock is 10 (wrong: expected paid).

findings.title: The hourly confirmation backlog can deadlock with a visitor re-signing up for a row it is about to queue (shared rate_limits rows)
findings.evidence: notify_confirm_backlog runs one transaction over up to 200 pending rows (147-158) and calls notify_confirm_queue for each: `select ... for update` on the notification row (100), then rate_limit_take on the address bucket (111) and the shared 'notify-confirm:all' bucket (114); rate_limit_take is an `insert ... on conflict do update` (contacts_and_email.sql:62-70), so each bucket row stays locked until commit. After its first queued mail the backlog holds the 'all' row and then locks the next notification row. notify_subscribe for that same address and variant locks the row in its upsert (212-222) and then, in notify_confirm_queue, waits for the 'all' row (114). Backlog waits on the notification row, the sign-up waits on the 'all' row: a cycle. The lock-order comment (30-34) names only the availability and notification rows. pg_cron serializes only instances of the same job, not a job against a visitor's request.
findings.impact: Precondition: a visitor whose confirmation a cap held back signs up again for the same variant in the sub-second window of the backlog run at minute 17. PostgreSQL aborts one side with 40P01: the visitor gets the generic 500 «تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.» (notify.ts maps every non-54000 error to FAILED), or the backlog's mails of that run roll back until the next hour.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the backlog never wait for a row: iterate `select n.id ... for update skip locked` (the row then re-locked by notify_confirm_queue is already its own), so a row a sign-up holds is left for that sign-up or the next hour.
findings.proof_recipe: Two pending rows N1 (address a1) and N2 (address a2, variant V2 out of stock) with confirm_sent_at null and the day's buckets free. Session A (postgres): begin; select finance.notify_confirm_queue('<N1>'); (holds the 'notify-confirm:all' row). Session B (service_role): select public.notify_subscribe(repeat('b',64), '<a2>', '<V2>', null); -> blocks on the 'all' row. Session A: select finance.notify_confirm_queue('<N2>'); -> one of the two sessions fails with SQLSTATE 40P01 (wrong: expected both to finish).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-OPS-02; round 8 rulings list 'the backlog against a sign-up for the same row at once' as uncovered

findings.title: A suppressed (bounced or complained) subscriber stays confirmed: every restock queues a notice that is closed 'suppressed' and sits in the mail attention list for good, and a sign-up of such an address spends a day's confirmation slot
findings.evidence: availability_sweep's `due` CTE updates every `n.status = 'confirmed' and n.notified_revision < v_revision` row and inserts one availability outbox row each (370-384) without reading finance.email_suppressions; notify_confirm_queue takes the address bucket and the day's 30 (111-116) before its insert, also for a suppressed address. outbox_claim then sets `status = 'suppressed'` with last_error untouched (order_emails.sql:277-282), and outbox_attention lists every 'suppressed' row whose last_error is not one of RECIPIENT_INACTIVE, NOT_PENDING, NOT_CONFIRMED, NO_FILE (order_emails.sql:421-423); outbox_replay refuses a suppressed recipient. No migration moves a public.notifications row on a bounce or a complaint.
findings.impact: After one hard bounce or complaint, each later restock of each variant the address confirmed adds an attention row in /admin/email that nobody can act on, burying the rows that matter (a buyer's receipt that bounced); a stranger can sign a known-bounced address up to burn one of the day's 30 confirmation mails each day.
findings.proposed_fix: Skip suppressed addresses where the mail is made: add `and not exists (select 1 from finance.email_suppressions s where s.recipient_hash = finance.recipient_hash(n.email))` to the sweep's due CTE, and return 'address' from notify_confirm_queue for a suppressed address before any bucket is taken.
findings.proof_recipe: With checkout on: a confirmed subscriber S of variant V (stock 0); insert into finance.email_suppressions (recipient_hash, reason) values (finance.recipient_hash('<S email>'), 'bounced'); set V's stock to 5; select finance.availability_sweep(); then select * from public.outbox_claim(1, 120, 100, 20, 3000, 30) and select * from public.outbox_attention() as the owner. Wrong result: the availability row for S is listed with status 'suppressed' and stays listed; every further false->true flip adds another.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-OPS-04

findings.title: The availability notice says the item is available («توفّر») also when the sweep fired on a preorder state
findings.evidence: availability_sweep counts the public state 'preorder' as sellable (notifications.sql:365: `finance.variant_public_state(r.variant_id) in ('available', 'preorder')`); notify_email_data (order_emails.sql:137-156) carries no state, date or note, and renderAvailability always writes «توفّر ... الذي طلبت أن نخبرك عنه.» (email.ts:519-521) with the product page link.
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner turns an out-of-stock variant with confirmed subscribers into a preorder (capacity and a future date). Subscribers are told the item is available; the page then offers «اطلب مسبقًا» with a delivery date weeks away. Dormant while preorder is off at opening (Q05).
findings.proposed_fix: Add the variant's public state (or `preorder` with its ships-on date) to notify_email_data and word a preorder notice as available to preorder with its date in renderAvailability.

findings.title: The per-address caps on confirmation mail key on the literal address, so one Gmail inbox can be sent the day's whole budget through dot and plus aliases
findings.evidence: notify_confirm_queue counts `o.recipient = v_note.email` for the five-in-30-days cap (104-108) and takes `finance.rate_limit_take('notify-confirm:email', finance.recipient_hash(v_note.email), 1, interval '1 day')` (111), where recipient_hash is sha256(lower(btrim(email))) (contacts_and_email.sql:151); notify.ts and the SQL accept '.' and '+' in the local part (`^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]{1,64}@...`). Gmail delivers every dotted variant and every +tag variant to the same inbox (support.google.com/mail/answer/7436150; support.google.com/a/users/answer/9282734), so victim+1@gmail.com, victim+2@gmail.com, v.ictim@gmail.com ... are each a fresh 'address' for both caps. What still binds is the shared 30-a-day total and the 5-an-hour caller throttle behind Turnstile.
findings.impact: A stranger with Turnstile passes and a few caller addresses can make the site mail one person's inbox up to 30 confirmation requests a day, every day (the per-address caps were built to stop exactly this, R8-06), and spends the day's 30 for every real visitor while doing it; complaints from the victim count against the sending domain at Resend.
findings.proposed_fix: Key both per-address caps on a canonical mailbox: a finance.mailbox_key(email) that lower-cases, drops a '+tag' from the local part and, for gmail.com and googlemail.com, drops dots; use it for the rate_limit_take key and compare it in the 30-day count (finance.mailbox_key(o.recipient) = finance.mailbox_key(v_note.email)).
findings.proof_recipe: With the day's buckets free and a published out-of-stock variant V: select public.notify_subscribe(repeat('c',64), 'victim+1@gmail.com', 'V', null); then the same with repeat('d',64) and 'victim+2@gmail.com', then 'v.ictim@gmail.com'. Wrong result: select count(*) from finance.email_outbox where kind = 'notify_confirm' and created_at > now() - interval '1 hour' and recipient in ('victim+1@gmail.com','victim+2@gmail.com','v.ictim@gmail.com') -> 3 mails to one Gmail inbox on one day (the per-address cap allows 1).
findings.prior_overlap: R8-06 (the per-address caps; this bypass is not recorded)

findings.title: A dispute's «سحب الملفات» can never be undone: a later «إبقاء الملفات» or a chargeback won leaves the paying buyer without his file, and no function restores an entitlement
findings.evidence: dispute_record with decision entitlement_revoked runs `perform finance.entitlements_revoke(v_order_id, v_items, 'dispute');` (550), which sets revoked_at (stats_disputes.sql:38-40); download_issue and download_redeem refuse a revoked entitlement (delivery.sql:311, 360). A follow-up row with entitlement_kept or direction for_seller only inserts a row (the decisions other than entitlement_revoked write nothing, and entitlement_kept may not even name items). No migration ever sets revoked_at back to null (grep of supabase/migrations: none), and the order view only shows the revocation (OrderView.tsx:791).
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner withdraws a digital item when a chargeback opens (the documented use of «سحب الملفات») and the chargeback is later decided for the seller, or the wrong line was ticked. The buyer paid and can never download what he bought again; the owner has no screen and no function to give the file back, only a refund or SQL as the migration role.
findings.proposed_fix: Make a follow-up with decision entitlement_kept on the same items restore them (`update finance.entitlements set revoked_at = null, revoke_reason = null where order_id = ... and order_item_id = any(items) and revoke_reason = 'dispute'`), audited like the revocation; a refund's revocation (reason 'refund') stays final.

findings.title: The buyer's access and erasure procedure never sends the operator to the contact-form steps for the same address, and the buyer functions read no contact message
findings.evidence: The buyer section opens «a buyer request touches customers, orders and their records only, never `auth.users`» (58) and its export and delete steps (60-88) name only privacy_buyer_export and privacy_buyer_erase; neither function reads or deletes public.contacts (stats_disputes.sql:606-830 has no reference to contacts). The contact-form messages of the same address are a separate section (44-48) with its own query and privacy_erase_contacts.

findings.proposed_fix: Add one line at the top of 'Handling a request': for any address, run every section that applies (contact-form visitor and buyer), and record each call in the ledger.

findings.title: fulfillment_update ships an item while a refund of that item is still in flight; order_resolve was given REFUND_IN_FLIGHT for the same race, shipping was not
findings.evidence: The only refund guard in fulfillment_update is ITEM_REFUNDED for an item that finance.item_fully_refunded already calls refunded (686-697), and item_fully_refunded counts `r.status = 'succeeded'` only (payment_core.sql:475-494). A refund in 'submitting' or 'uncertain' that allocates the whole line does not stop `update finance.fulfillments ... set state = 'shipped'` (708-719) nor the order_shipped mail. The round 7b ruling added REFUND_IN_FLIGHT to order_resolve (953-961) because a line committed while its refund was in flight 'could never ship'; tests/integration/order-operations.test.ts:1759-1789 accepts 'shipped, then refunded' as a valid end state of the ship-versus-refund race.
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner refunds a line that has not shipped (a buyer who cancelled, a damaged copy) and the refund is still submitting or uncertain (seconds, or until the job settles an uncertain one) when an operations member ships it from the to-ship list. The buyer gets the money back and the book; the order view shows no warning to the person shipping.
findings.proposed_fix: Before the moves, answer REFUND_IN_FLIGHT (with itemIds) when a refund of the order in 'submitting' or 'uncertain' names one of the items in its allocation (or is unallocated), as order_resolve does; the owner's in-flight refund is decided within minutes.
findings.proof_recipe: A paid order with one physical line: reserve a refund of the whole line with refund_request (status 'submitting') and do not settle it; as operations call public.fulfillment_update('<order>', array['<item>']::uuid[], 'shipped', 'SMSA', 'T1', null). Wrong result: {ok:true, changed:1} and an order_shipped mail queued; then refund_result(..., 'succeeded', ...) leaves the item shipped and refunded.
findings.prior_overlap: orchestrator's own round 7b finding (REFUND_IN_FLIGHT for order_resolve only)
