findings.title: A routine policy publish closes checkout for every buyer while the owner's screen still says «الشراء مفتوح», and nothing alerts the owner
findings.evidence: commerce_settings_get() returns the raw switch: `'checkoutEnabled', v_row.checkout_enabled,`. Since P08 the buyer's quote reports the effective state (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:352-356: `v_settings.checkout_enabled and ... and v_settings.policy_revisions <> '{}'::jsonb`). policies_reset_approval (20260930120000_audit_fixes.sql:141-149) empties policy_revisions on any new seq of an approved policy and writes only an owner-only audit row 'commerce.policies_reset'; it queues no finance.owner_alert (the only callers of owner_alert are payment, refund and order code). src/components/admin/CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:251 renders `{row.checkoutEnabled ? 'الشراء مفتوح' : 'الشراء مغلق'}` from that raw value; AdminHome reads 'content.publish_due_failed' audit rows but not 'commerce.policies_reset', and orders_alerts (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:473-521) has no checkout-readiness count; PublishBar has no warning for policies.
findings.impact: After checkout opens, an editor (or the owner) fixes a typo in «سياسة الاسترجاع» and publishes: from that moment every buyer's cart and checkout show checkout unavailable, no order can be placed, and the owner gets no mail and no home alert; his commerce screen keeps saying «الشراء مفتوح» under the switch. Sales stay closed until he happens to notice «لم تُعتمد بعد» and re-approves with TOTP. A scheduled policy publish (publish_due) does the same at an hour nobody is watching. The same mismatch follows a settings save that clears the seller name or registration while checkout is on: commerce_settings_save (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:14-78) does not refuse it, unlike commerce_checkout_set.
findings.proposed_fix: Return the effective state from commerce_settings_get (for example 'checkoutOpen' = checkout_enabled and seller set and policy_revisions <> '{}', plus a reason) and show «الشراء مغلق: السياسات تحتاج اعتمادًا» on the commerce screen; in policies_reset_approval call finance.owner_alert('policies_reset', v_doc || ':' || v_seq, ...) when it resets while checkout_enabled is true (alert_email_data needs the matching text); optionally warn in PublishBar before publishing a new seq of an approved policy.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 GAP-G1-2 (refuted, pre-P08) asked to tell the owner; P08 since fixed the buyer side (I48.2, quote readiness) and added the switch display that now shows the raw value

findings.title: Once a staff address is suppressed, every contact notice to it ends 'suppressed' with no signal and no way back, and D31 leaves no other inbox
findings.evidence: outbox_claim (final) suppresses by recipient hash for every kind, staff mail included: `update finance.email_outbox o set status = 'suppressed' ... where o.status in ('pending', 'uncertain') and exists (select 1 from finance.email_suppressions s where s.recipient_hash = finance.recipient_hash(o.recipient));`. A hash enters email_suppressions on any non-temporary bounce, a complaint or a provider 'email.suppressed' event (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:646-659), with no expiry and no function to lift it. outbox_replay accepts only 'exhausted' or 'uncertain' (order_emails.sql:378), so a suppressed row can never be queued again; AdminHome counts only replayable rows (src/components/admin/AdminHome.tsx:101-103, 'Suppressed recipients ... never clear, so counting them left a number the owner could not bring back'); public.contacts has no grant for any API role, the owner included (DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:23).
findings.impact: With the owner as the only active owner or operations recipient (one notice per message), one hard bounce or a provider suppression of the owner's address (for example while the anas.studio mail domain is being set up, or the owner pressing «spam» on a junk contact notice in a mailbox that sends complaint reports, which email_event_record turns into a suppression) makes every later contact notice to him end as 'suppressed' at the next claim. The visitor reads «وصلت رسالتك. شكراً لك.» (src/components/public/contact/ContactForm.tsx:126), the message sits in public.contacts that no admin screen can read, the owner home shows no problem, and only the «انتهت» filter of /admin/email lists the rows. Removing the suppression by hand does not bring them back (no replay of 'suppressed'), and finance.contacts_purge never deletes those messages because no notice was ever sent. The same happens to owner_alert mail, which the orders alerts on the home partly cover.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat staff-recipient kinds differently: in outbox_claim exhaust (not suppress) a contact_notice or owner_alert whose active staff recipient is suppressed, with last_error 'RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED', so the home counts it; let outbox_replay accept a 'suppressed' row once its hash is no longer in finance.email_suppressions; and give the owner a staff-only function that lists suppressed active staff addresses (and lifts one, audited), surfaced as a banner on the owner home.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-11 (extended: the dead end after un-suppression); lead:DB-CORE-08 (messages kept for ever)

findings.title: Policy approval and a concurrent policy publish can commit an approval of the old seq with no reset, leaving checkout stuck on POLICY_CHANGED
findings.evidence: policies_reset_approval (AFTER ROW on published_documents) only touches the settings row when its WHERE matches: `update finance.commerce_settings set policy_revisions = '{}'::jsonb ... where id = 1 and policy_revisions ? v_doc and (policy_revisions ->> v_doc) is distinct from v_seq::text;`. When policy_revisions does not yet hold the doc (first approval, or any approval after a reset, which clears the whole object), the WHERE is false and no row lock is taken. commerce_policies_approve (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:104-115) locks the settings row FOR UPDATE and then reads `select seq ... from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store'` under READ COMMITTED, which cannot see the publisher's uncommitted upsert.
findings.impact: Interleaving: an editor's publish_version (or publish_due) of policies/store seq N+1 runs its trigger while revisions = {} (no reset, no lock); the owner's approval reads the committed seq N and commits {store: N}; the publish commits. Approved = N, live and next build = N+1, and no commerce.policies_reset row. Every buyer page built from N+1 sends store N+1, checkout_create (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:462) answers POLICY_CHANGED and the checkout form shows the stale-policy state on every reload, until the owner notices and approves again; the admin shows only the approved revisions, not the live ones. Window is the few milliseconds of the publish transaction, so likelihood is low; no buyer consents to unapproved text.
findings.proposed_fix: In policies_reset_approval, for a policies row take the settings row lock unconditionally before the conditional update (`perform 1 from finance.commerce_settings where id = 1 for update;`), so a publish and an approval of policies serialize: either the approval waits and reads the new seq, or the trigger waits and then sees the approved N and resets.
findings.proof_recipe: Two psql sessions as postgres on a stack with checkout configured and policy_revisions = '{}': S1: begin; select set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"<editor id>","role":"authenticated"}', true); set local role authenticated; insert a new policies/store version (next seq) and select public.publish_version('policies','store',<seq>); -- do not commit. S2: select public.commerce_policies_approve('<owner id>', <current version>); -- returns at once with store = old seq. S1: commit. Then select policy_revisions from finance.commerce_settings -> {store: old seq}, published_documents store seq = new seq, and no audit_events row 'commerce.policies_reset' after S2. Expected correct result: either S2 approves the new seq or the reset fires.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 GAP-G5-3 (confirmed/low, filed under ISSUES I48.1): not fixed; P08 consent check (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:462) turns its wrong-consent outcome into a POLICY_CHANGED dead end, so the earlier fix holds only partly

findings.title: outbox_attention's 200-row cap fills up with rows nobody can act on, which pushes older replayable mail out of the admin
findings.evidence: `where (o.status in ('exhausted', 'uncertain', 'suppressed') or o.delivery in ('bounced', 'complained', 'failed')) and coalesce(o.last_error, '') not in (...) order by o.created_at desc limit 200;` Suppressed rows and sent rows with a bounce, complaint or failure never leave this set (no time bound, no purge of sent buyer mail per docs/privacy-data-map.md:11), and they sort among the replayable ones by created_at only. EmailView lists exactly this result and AdminHome's count is computed over it (AdminHome.tsx:183-188, `capped` at 200).
findings.impact: As a live shop accumulates bounced addresses and their later suppressed mail, the newest 200 problem rows become mostly ended ones; an exhausted or uncertain receipt or order link older than them disappears from /admin/email and from the home count, so nobody can find it to replay it, and the buyer never gets the mail. Slow to arrive at a small shop's volume, silent when it does.
findings.proposed_fix: Order the replayable rows first (`order by (o.status in ('exhausted','uncertain')) desc, o.created_at desc`), or bound the ended rows by age (for example the last 30 days) so the cap only ever trims what is past acting on.
findings.prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1 L6 added the «+» for the cap, not the ordering)

findings.title: service_role's default table privileges are never revoked, so it may hold DELETE and TRUNCATE on the append-only and content tables the migrations describe as insert-only
findings.evidence: The only default-privilege revokes name anon and authenticated: `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated;` (and sequences, functions). 20260925090000_audit_and_staff_directory.sql:77-82 then grants service_role `select, insert, update` on staff and `insert` on audit_events and states 'No delete on either table'. artifacts/acceptance/P03/commands.txt:44-46 recorded the local pg_default_acl for postgres granting service_role 'Delete/Truncate/References/Trigger' on every new relation; Supabase changelog 45329 says projects with the legacy 'expose new tables' setting grant select, insert, update, delete to service_role on every new public table until the setting is applied (2026-10-30). The append-only trigger is `before update or delete ... for each row` (20260925090000:36-38) and has no TRUNCATE counterpart.
findings.impact: What service_role can do to audit_events, staff, contacts, media, content_versions and published_documents depends on the project's default ACL at creation, not on the migrations: a holder of the service key (every Edge Function) can, for example, `DELETE /rest/v1/published_documents` with no filter and wipe the live site, or empty contacts and media, with no audit row; a TRUNCATE of audit_events bypasses the append-only trigger for any role that holds it. Bounded: the key lives only in Supabase, and its holder can already insert an owner staff row.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables from service_role;` (and sequences), revoke delete, truncate, references, trigger on the existing slice tables from service_role, keep only the explicit grants, and add `create trigger audit_events_no_truncate before truncate on public.audit_events for each statement execute function public.audit_events_immutable();`.
findings.proof_recipe: Locally and on the hosted project: select table_name, privilege_type from information_schema.role_table_grants where grantee = 'service_role' and table_schema = 'public' and table_name in ('audit_events','staff','contacts','media','content_versions','published_documents','media_upload_tickets') order by 1,2; and select * from pg_default_acl where defaclrole = 'postgres'::regrole. Wrong result: any DELETE, TRUNCATE, TRIGGER or REFERENCES row (or SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE beyond staff and audit_events INSERT).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-03; AUDIT-1 S01.5 fixed the PUBLIC function default only

findings.title: media_is_published(uuid) stays executable by anon although no policy or code calls it any more
findings.evidence: `grant execute on function public.media_is_published(uuid) to anon;` survives both `create or replace` (20260927180000:10, 20260930120000:96). The media policy now uses media_published_ids() (20260930120000:89-92); there is no policy on storage.objects in any migration, and a search of src/, supabase/functions/ and scripts/ finds no caller (only tests/integration/audit-fixes.test.ts:125 and :207, which pin it). The comment at 20260930120000:94-95 still justifies it with 'storage policies and the admin still call it'.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated RPC that runs jsonb_path_exists over every published document (plus the products table) per call: an oracle for 'is this uuid referenced anywhere public' and a per-request CPU cost an anonymous caller can repeat at will, for no product use.
findings.proposed_fix: `revoke execute on function public.media_is_published(uuid) from anon;` and update the S01.5 test's expected anon list to catalog_availability and media_published_ids.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-05; AUDIT-1 S02.4 (fix kept the grant)

findings.title: outbox_replay treats a null p_accept_duplicate_risk as consent past the 23-hour window
findings.evidence: `v_ambiguous := o.first_attempt_at <= now() - interval '23 hours'; if v_ambiguous and not p_accept_duplicate_risk then raise ...` With p_accept_duplicate_risk null the condition is null, the IF does not fire, and the UPDATE rotates the key (`case when v_ambiguous then gen_random_uuid()`); the audit row stores acceptedDuplicateRisk: null. The function is granted to authenticated (order_emails.sql:444). The admin always sends a boolean (src/components/admin/EmailView.tsx:95).
findings.impact: A direct call by an owner or operations member with {"p_id": N, "p_accept_duplicate_risk": null} replays a mail that may already have been delivered, with a fresh idempotency key and no recorded acceptance, against DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:91 ('An ambiguous send outside that lifetime needs reconciliation before retry'). A buyer can get a receipt or order link twice; the trail cannot tell who accepted the risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `if v_ambiguous and not coalesce(p_accept_duplicate_risk, false) then` (or reject a null argument outright).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-06; AUDIT-1 X1.3 added v_ambiguous

findings.title: Build-time loaders read published posts and taxonomies without paging, so PostgREST's 1000-row cap would silently drop content
findings.evidence: `fetch(`${...}/rest/v1/published_documents?${params}`, { headers: { apikey } })` with params `collection=eq.posts&select=doc_id,data,first_published_at` and no Range header or paging; the body is accepted whenever `response.ok`. supabase/config.toml:18 sets `max_rows = 1000` (the hosted default is the same), above which PostgREST answers 200 with the first 1000 rows.
findings.impact: Once the journal or the tag list passes 1000 published documents, the next build drops the rest without an error: posts vanish from the journal and their pages 404 after the deploy. Far off for one author's journal; recorded because the failure is silent.
findings.proposed_fix: Send `Prefer: count=exact` and fail the build when Content-Range's total exceeds the rows received (or page with Range), in journal.ts and any other published_documents list loader.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-07

findings.title: A contact message whose notice never reaches a staff mailbox is kept for ever, unread and unreadable
findings.evidence: finance.contacts_purge selects only contacts with a notice `o.status = 'sent' ... and o.sent_at < now() - interval '90 days'`. A notice swept as RECIPIENT_INACTIVE (the recipient demoted or revoked before the claim, 20261002120000_order_emails.sql:284-301) can never be replayed (order_emails.sql:367-377) and is hidden from outbox_attention (:423); an exhausted notice stays until someone replays it; a suppressed one can never be replayed (DB-CORE-02). public.contacts has no grant for any API role, so no screen shows these messages.
findings.impact: The visitor's name, email and message stay in public.contacts indefinitely, against D36's 90 days (docs/privacy-data-map.md:9 says 'kept until one does' for exactly this case, but nothing can ever make it happen), and the visitor is never answered. Precondition: a team change between submit and claim, an outage spanning eight attempts, or a suppressed staff address.
findings.proposed_fix: Give such messages a terminal retention rule in contacts_purge (for example: also purge a contact 90 days after it was created when none of its notices is pending, sending or uncertain), or re-queue a RECIPIENT_INACTIVE notice to the current owner; the period is E08's to approve.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-08; D36

findings.title: The last-owner guard's concurrency claim has no test: only sequential demotions are exercised
findings.evidence: 20260924130000_staff_and_app_server.sql:52-76 promises that two concurrent demotions of the last two owners cannot both pass (deferred constraint trigger plus pg_advisory_xact_lock under READ COMMITTED). The only test (staff-admin.test.ts:106-132) demotes one owner after pausing the others, on one connection. Reading the code the claim holds: the trigger function is volatile, so its EXISTS takes a fresh snapshot after the lock, which the first committer holds until commit.
findings.impact: None found; the invariant 'the last active owner cannot be removed or demoted' (DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:9) rests on reasoning alone, so a later change to the trigger (for example making it STABLE, or dropping the lock) would not be caught.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an integration test with two pg clients: each begins, demotes a different one of the only two active owners, then both commit; exactly one commit must fail with 23514.
findings.proof_recipe: Two psql sessions as postgres with exactly two active owners A and B: S1: begin; update public.staff set role = 'editor' where user_id = 'A'; S2: begin; update public.staff set role = 'editor' where user_id = 'B'; S1: commit; S2: commit; -> expected S2 fails with 23514 'At least one active owner is required.'; wrong result: both commit and select count(*) from public.staff where role = 'owner' and active returns 0.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-10; AUDIT-2 GAP-G1-8 (refuted)

findings.title: Edits to a library image's name, folder, alt text, caption and rights leave no audit row
findings.evidence: `grant update (name, folder, alt_ar, caption, rights) on public.media to authenticated;` with media_staff_update for owner and editor and only the media_touch trigger; media_rename_folder (:164-184) is security invoker with no audit insert. The only media audit rows are media.create and media.delete.
findings.impact: An editor can rewrite an image's rights statement (a required provenance record, DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:95) or its public alt text (anon reads alt_ar since 20260930140000:376), which reaches the site at the next build without a publish, and nobody can later see who changed it or what it said.
findings.proposed_fix: An AFTER UPDATE trigger on public.media that inserts a media.update audit row naming the changed columns (values for rights, as catalog_audit does for money columns).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-CORE-12

findings.title: The contact retention purge leaves no trace: no count-only audit row and no job run, so a failing purge goes unnoticed
findings.evidence: finance.contacts_purge (lines 191-227) deletes contacts and their outbox rows and returns a count, with no insert into public.audit_events; its siblings do write one (buyer_retention_purge 'privacy.buyer_retention', notifications_purge, payment_events_purge). The job is scheduled as plain SQL (`select cron.schedule('contacts-purge', '29 3 * * *', 'select finance.contacts_purge()')`, line 229), so its outcome lands only in cron.job_run_details, which is purged after 7 days (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:820-823); the owner home lists finance.job_runs only (job_runs_latest). docs/privacy-data-map.md:29 says 'the purges and the buyer erase write count-only rows'.
findings.impact: Nobody can show that the D36 90-day deletion ran, and if the purge starts failing (a lock timeout, a later constraint) contact messages are kept past the promised period with no signal anywhere the owner looks. The same blind spot covers the other pure-SQL nightly purges (rate-limits, buyer-retention, notifications, payment-events).
findings.proposed_fix: Have contacts_purge insert a count-only 'privacy.contacts_purge' audit row when it deletes something, and record each nightly SQL purge in finance.job_runs (a small wrapper that calls the purge in a begin/exception block and writes ok/failed), so job_runs_latest shows a failing purge.
findings.prior_overlap: none

coverage:
READ IN FULL: the eleven slice migrations (20260924130000 through 20260929120000) and every later statement that alters their objects: 20260927170000_policy_approval, 20260927180000_store_media, 20260930120000_audit_fixes (all), 20260930140000_audit2_fixes (all), 20260930130000_buyer_retention, 20261002120000_order_emails (1-120 and 230-449: final outbox_claim/replay/attention), 20261002100000_payment_core (30-75 outbox kinds, 420-435 owner_alert), 20261002170000_stats_disputes (236-330, 590-890: buyer_retention_purge, privacy_buyer_export/erase), 20260927160000 (1-60, 1085-1120), 20261002145000 (require_staff, orders_alerts), 20261002110000 (quote readiness 340-362, checkout switch 725-745); plus a grep of every later migration for policies, triggers, FKs, grants, storage, cron, vault, net, views and RLS touching the slice (no other alteration exists). supabase/config.toml, seed.sql, templates/magic_link.html, PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md, PLANS/ISSUES.md, docs/privacy-data-map.md (1-100), docs/operations.md (160-330). Interplay code: staff-admin/index.ts, _shared/staff.ts, recent-totp.ts, jobs.ts, outbox.ts (30-70, 230-330), admin.ts (dispatch 217-252, storage keys), EmailView.tsx (40-140), AdminHome.tsx (attention, publish failures, alerts), CommerceSettingsForm.tsx (150-290), src/lib/content.ts (70-160), journal.ts, policies.ts, store.ts (1-130), collections policies/scenes/rooms/index. Tests: staff, staff-admin, cron-jobs, audit-fixes (100-215), forms (189-270) in full; case lists of outbox, static-site, media-security, email-delivery, privacy-requests, policy-approval, commerce-settings. Prior audits: AUDIT-2 findings.json (hidden items, X-SEC-1/2, GAP-G5-3, GAP-G1-2), AUDIT-1 REPORT G4.2, P08 round-05 uncovered list, P03 commands.txt default-ACL note.
OBJECT PICTURE: every public table of the slice has RLS on; anon reads published_documents (hidden posts filtered) and media id/derivatives/alt_ar of public ids only; authenticated reads staff (own row, owner all), audit_events (owner), content_versions and content_documents (owner/editor, view is security_invoker), media (owner/editor) and inserts content_versions (four columns, author = auth.uid()); no API role updates or deletes staff, audit_events, content_versions, published_documents, contacts or tickets except service_role's undeclared defaults (DB-CORE-05). finance has no USAGE for any API role. Static ACL model re-run over all 27 migrations: 159 functions, none PUBLIC-executable, all definers set search_path=''; anon executes 3 functions; p_actor is caller-supplied only in service_role functions, fed from the verified JWT. aal is never read in SQL: aal2/TOTP lives only in the Edge Functions, and no authenticated-granted function in the slice performs an aal2 action. findings.title: A digital line can be bought in quantity 2-20 but grants exactly one entitlement: the buyer pays N times for one download licence
findings.evidence: checkout_price accepts any line with `if v_qty < 1 or v_qty > 20` (line 91) whatever the fulfilment, and charges `price_halalas * v_qty` (line 141). order_try_commit (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:699-705) inserts ONE entitlement per order item (`finance.entitlements.order_item_id` is UNIQUE, `on conflict (order_item_id) do nothing`), and download_issue (20261002140000_delivery.sql:314-319) caps tokens per entitlement (10/day, 3 uses each), never per unit. The product page's AddToCart (src/components/store/AddToCart.tsx:56-66, used by VariantAction for every variant) offers 1-20 for any variant and addLine merges a second click into quantity 2.
findings.impact: A buyer who clicks «أضف إلى السلة» twice on the ebook (or types 2 meaning a gift) is charged 2x price for one non-transferable entitlement and one set of download links; the receipt and order page say ×2. The only remedy is a manual partial refund by the owner after a complaint.
findings.proposed_fix: In finance.checkout_price, after the variant is read, add `if v_row.fulfillment = 'digital' and v_qty <> 1 then INVALID_QUANTITY` (one licence per order line), and have AddToCart/CartView show no quantity field (fixed 1) for a digital variant. If multi-copy gifting is wanted instead, it needs N entitlements and a transfer flow, which nothing builds.
findings.prior_overlap: none found in AUDIT-1/AUDIT-2/P08 rounds

findings.title: No per-resource unpaid-hold limit: one address holds 200 units of a scarce variant for 20 minutes an hour (about 60 continuously), three hold them around the clock; the recorded residual understates it
findings.evidence: Final checkout_create keeps only: the session advisory lock + 'one unexpired pending order per checkout_session' (lines 483-498; the session id is a client-chosen UUID, sessionStorage per tab, src/lib/cart.ts:474-478), the IP throttle `rate_limit_take('checkout:ip', p_ip_hash, 10, interval '1 hour')` (line 479) and the store-wide 500/day (line 532). Each order may hold 20 units per line (checkout_price line 91) and 50 lines. clientKeyHash (supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limit.ts:41-69) keys IPv6 per /64, so a /48 is 65,536 buckets. DATA-AND-SECURITY 'Unpaid reservation abuse' asks for 'transactionally enforced active-hold limits by guest checkout session and normalized recipient/resource'; P08 removed the recipient limit (contract 13.1) and no resource limit exists. docs/operations.md:653-654 and 1161-1162 record only 'many sessions from many addresses can still hold scarce stock for 20 minutes at a time'.
findings.impact: Arithmetic from the code: one IPv4 address (or one IPv6 /64) passing Turnstile in a real browser gets 10 creates per clock hour, each holding up to 20 units of one variant for 20 minutes, so it holds 200 units for 20 minutes every hour, or about 60 units continuously by spreading the 10 creates. Three addresses keep 200 units held around the clock, so at the launch of a signed edition of 150-200 copies buyers read «الكمية محجوزة مؤقتًا لطلب آخر؛ حاول بعد قليل.» all day; the same three addresses also spend the store-wide 500 a day in about 17 hours and close checkout for every buyer until 00:00 UTC. An IPv6 /48 is 65,536 throttle buckets, so only Turnstile bounds it. The record says 'many sessions from many addresses', so the owner accepted a smaller risk than the built one.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a resource limit inside checkout_create under the variant locks it already holds: e.g. refuse (OUT_OF_STOCK held) when the units of a stocked or preorder variant held by other unexpired unpaid orders would exceed a ceiling (a fixed share of stock, or a per-order cap such as 5 units of a signed/physical variant), and/or an active pending-order cap per IP hash (store ip_hash on finance.orders, advisory-lock it like the session). At minimum correct operations.md and contract 13.1 with the concrete numbers (200 units per address per window, /64 buckets) so the acceptance is informed.
findings.prior_overlap: Recorded residual in P08-CONTRACT 13.1 and docs/operations.md (worse than recorded); AUDIT-2 X-SEC-4 removed the per-email limit

findings.title: Switching a preorder off strands its in-flight and unresolved orders: the commit checks the reservation's preorder flag against a capacity the form has just nulled
findings.evidence: order_try_commit: `if r.res_preorder then v_free := coalesce(r.preorder_capacity, 0) - finance.preorder_committed(r.variant_id) - case when v_own then 0 else finance.active_holds(r.variant_id) end;` (lines 648-650), where res_preorder is the reservation snapshot and preorder_capacity the variant's current value. The variant form sends `preorder_capacity: preorder ? (values.preorder_capacity ?? null) : null` (src/admin/tables/variants.ts:97), so after «طلب مسبق» is switched off v_free = 0 - committed < quantity. order_resolve calls the same function (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:963) and answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE. tests/integration/payment.test.ts:1664-1673 pins exactly this outcome. docs/operations.md:1083-1089 tells the owner to switch the preorder off when the copies arrive and says nothing about open holds or unresolved orders.
findings.impact: Precondition: a buyer holds an unpaid preorder reservation (20-minute window, or a payment in 3-D Secure) or a preorder order sits in paid_needs_resolution when the owner switches the preorder off, the documented step when the copies arrive. The paid order lands in paid_needs_resolution although copies are on the shelf, and «حلّ الطلب» answers STOCK_UNAVAILABLE for ever; the only exits are a refund or switching the preorder back on with a capacity, which nothing tells the owner.
findings.proposed_fix: In finance.order_try_commit treat a preorder-flagged reservation whose variant is no longer a preorder by the stock rule (join v.preorder and use `r.res_preorder and v.preorder` in the free check and in the decrement loop's preorder test), and add to docs/operations.md 'Preorders' that held and unresolved preorder orders exist when switching off. Alternatively keep the capacity when the switch goes off and say so in the form.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-COMMERCE-01

findings.title: The commit stock-checks and decrements a line by the variant's current stock column, not by the line's snapshot or reservation
findings.evidence: First loop: `elsif r.stock is not null then v_free := r.stock - ...` with r.stock = v.stock of the variant now (lines 638-652); decrement loop `where i.order_id = p_order and v.stock is not null and not coalesce(x.preorder, false)` (line 676) over a LEFT JOIN on reservations, never i.fulfillment or x.id. checkout_create inserts a reservation only for non-digital or preorder lines (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:611). The owner may change fulfillment and stock through the Data API (grant update on product_variants, 20260927160000:284-285) and the variant form offers the fulfilment select (src/admin/tables/variants.ts:22-28).
findings.impact: Precondition: the owner changes a digital variant (without a file) to physical, or a physical one to digital, while an unpaid order of it exists. A digital line is then refused for stock (paid_needs_resolution) or takes one physical copy out of stock while the buyer gets a file; a physical line becomes stock-free (no check, no decrement) while a fulfilment row still asks operations to ship a copy. Rare and owner-caused, but stock and fulfilment then disagree silently.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive both loops by the reservation: inner `join finance.inventory_reservations x` (or `where x.id is not null`) and decide by x.preorder; a line without a reservation needs no stock. Optionally refuse a fulfilment change on a variant with unpaid or unresolved lines.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-COMMERCE-02

findings.title: commerce_policies_approve still reads the live policy seqs without the per-document lock, so an approval overlapping a publish records a replaced seq and silently closes checkout
findings.evidence: Final body: after `select * into v_row from finance.commerce_settings where id = 1 for update`, four plain `select seq into v_store from public.published_documents where collection = 'policies' and doc_id = 'store'` (lines 112-115). Publishers take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:' || collection || ':' || doc_id))` (publish_version audit_fixes.sql:177, publish_due audit2_fixes.sql:311) but the approval does not. policies_reset_approval updates the settings row only `where policy_revisions ? v_doc` (audit_fixes.sql:141-145), so while revisions are '{}' (any approval after a reset) a concurrent publish of seq N+1 matches no row, takes no lock, and the approval commits {doc: N}.
findings.impact: Precondition: a policy publish (manual, or publish_due at the minute) commits during the owner's approval call. The approval names a seq that is no longer live; after the next build every create sends the built seq and gets POLICY_CHANGED (the form says the policies are being updated) while the quote still answers checkoutEnabled true, and no commerce.policies_reset row or alert tells the owner why sales stopped.
findings.proposed_fix: At the top of commerce_policies_approve, before the `for update` of finance.commerce_settings, take the publishers' advisory locks in a fixed order: `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:policies:' || d)) from unnest(array['delivery','privacy','refund','store']) d;`. They must come first: a publisher holds its document lock and then updates the settings row in policies_reset_approval, so taking them after the row lock would deadlock.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 GAP-G5-3 (in ISSUES I48 item 1; the DB race was not fixed, only its effect changed); lead:DB-COMMERCE-03

findings.title: Coupon uses and committed preorder units are counted across test and live, so hosted sandbox runs spend live coupon limits and preorder capacity for good
findings.evidence: finance.coupon_uses: `from finance.coupon_redemptions c where c.coupon_id = p_coupon_id and (c.state = 'committed' or ...)` with no join to the order's environment (lines 445-455); finance.preorder_committed (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:439-448) and finance.active_holds likewise. order_try_commit commits the redemption and the reservations of a test order like a live one, and decrements real stock. A paid test order is never purged (order_erasable requires expired or cancelled) and a refund releases preorder reservations but never a coupon redemption (20261002170000_stats_disputes.sql:200-206). docs/payments-runbook.md 'Before live' (lines 312-316) says only 'read the stock', and its line 209 says 'every SQL entry point ... refuses work on an order or an attempt of the other one'.
findings.impact: Precondition: the supervised sandbox on the hosted site (planned, test mode behind PAYMENTS_TEST_ACCESS_CODE) pays orders with the launch coupon or a preorder variant. On the live site that coupon answers COUPON_EXHAUSTED N uses early and the preorder offers N fewer units; the variant form counts the test units among «طلبات مسبقة مؤكدة لم تُشحن», asking Anas to net phantom preorders out of real stock. No admin path removes a test redemption.
findings.proposed_fix: Count by mode: join finance.orders o on o.id = order_id and o.environment = the request's or order's environment in coupon_uses, preorder_committed and active_holds (checkout_price gets the environment from checkout_create/quote), or at least add to the runbook's 'Before live': use a separate coupon and preorder variant for the sandbox and recreate both before going live.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-COMMERCE-05

findings.title: The customer profile keeps the name and phone of whoever first typed the address at checkout, paid or not, for as long as any order of it exists
findings.evidence: `insert into public.customers (email, name, phone) values (v_email, v_name, v_phone) on conflict (email) do nothing;` (lines 538-541) runs at create, before any payment, and nothing later writes the profile (only the owner's Data API update of name/phone). The admin «العملاء» list shows exactly these columns (src/admin/tables/customers.ts:25-30) and links them to the address's orders; privacy_buyer_export returns them as the person's 'customer' record (20261002170000_stats_disputes.sql:624-627). The retention purge keeps the profile while any order references it (paid orders are kept for accounting).
findings.impact: Anyone who knows an address can open (and abandon) one order with it under any name and phone; when the real owner of the address later buys, the profile shown to the staff, and exported to the buyer on an access request, carries the stranger's name and phone for years. Fulfilment is safe (the order view reads the order's own snapshot), so the harm is a misleading customers list and a polluted export.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the profile from paid orders only: move the upsert from checkout_create into order_try_commit (or apply_verified_payment) as `on conflict (email) do update set name = excluded.name, phone = coalesce(excluded.phone, customers.phone)`, keeping checkout_create's customer_id by inserting a bare row (email only, name from the order) when none exists; or show the latest paid order's contact in the list instead of the profile's.
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: Every product save requests a site build, including a draft product, an unchanged save and a stale save that matched no row
findings.evidence: `create trigger products_request_build after insert or delete or update of slug, title, summary, body, cover_image, status, sort_order on public.products for each statement execute function public.catalog_request_build();` (lines 245-247) is never replaced (grep of all migrations). A statement-level UPDATE OF trigger fires whenever a listed column is in the SET list, changed or not, and even when the statement updates zero rows. The product form always sends all seven columns (src/admin/tables/products.ts:43-51) with `.eq('version', ...)` (src/components/admin/TableForm.tsx:217-222). AUDIT-2 DB-catalog-1 fixed exactly this for product_variants (audit2_fixes.sql:793-815, then payment_core.sql:75-86) but not for products.
findings.impact: While Anas builds the catalog, each save of a draft (not public), each re-save and each version conflict asks for a Pages build (coalesced to one per two minutes by site_build_trigger). Cloudflare Pages Free allows 500 builds per month (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/), the budget I32(3) asks to watch; draft-catalog work can spend a visible share of it for no public change.
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror the variant fix: keep the statement trigger for insert and delete only, and add `after update ... for each row when ((old.slug, old.title, old.summary, old.body, old.cover_image, old.status, old.sort_order) is distinct from (new.slug, new.title, new.summary, new.body, new.cover_image, new.status, new.sort_order) and (old.status = 'published' or new.status = 'published'))`. The variant row trigger (payment_core.sql:76-86) has the same draft blind spot: a price edit on a variant of a draft product also requests a build; a guard in catalog_request_build for row calls (`tg_level = 'ROW'` and the product not published: return) would cover it.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 DB-catalog-1 (same class, fixed for variants only)

findings.title: A coupon code typed with Arabic-Indic digits is refused as invalid: the code is folded for case and spaces only
findings.evidence: `v_code text := nullif(upper(btrim(coalesce(p_coupon_code, ''))), '');` (checkout_price line 56; the same in checkout_create line 415) is compared with coupons.code, whose check is `^[A-Z0-9]{3,32}$` (20260927160000:156). The client folds case only (`normalizeCoupon = text.trim().toUpperCase()`, src/lib/cart.ts:358-360) and so does the function (supabase/functions/_shared/checkout.ts:419), while the phone and OTP fields fold U+0660-U+0669 and U+06F0-U+06F9 to ASCII (src/lib/digits.ts:13-16).
findings.impact: A buyer who types the digits of «EID25» on the Arabic layout (EID٢٥) gets «كود الخصم غير صالح.» for a valid code and pays full price or gives up; the message suggests the code itself is wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Fold the digits in the one SQL normalization both functions use: `translate(upper(btrim(p_coupon_code)), '٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹', '01234567890123456789')` in checkout_price and checkout_create (and the same fold in normalizeCoupon so the field shows what is sent).
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: Bidi override and isolate characters pass the name, address and dedication checks; the displays contain them, so only the buyer's own value is affected
findings.evidence: checkout_create refuses `v_name ~ '[[:cntrl:]]'` (line 471) and `v_address ~ '[[:cntrl:]]'` (line 520); checkout_price refuses a dedication with the same class (line 119). The function's own rule is `!/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]/` (supabase/functions/_shared/commerce-settings.ts:18), so U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 (format characters, not controls) pass the function; whether the database class also lets them through depends on the hosted collation provider. The admin wraps each value in <bdi> (src/components/admin/OrderView.tsx:408, 413, 441) and the mail renderer removes \p{Bidi_Control} (supabase/functions/_shared/email.ts:337-338).
findings.impact: A buyer who pastes an override into their own name, address or dedication sees it rendered reversed inside its isolate on the order view and the signed checklist (a dedication or address copied by hand could be miscopied); the isolation and the mail stripping keep it from reordering anything around it, so there is no cross-order spoofing.
findings.proposed_fix: Optional hardening: add the ranges U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 to noControlCharacters and to the SQL checks (`~ '[[:cntrl:]‪-‮⁦-⁩]'`), leaving ZWJ/ZWNJ and LRM/RLM alone.
findings.proof_recipe: On the local stack: `select E'‮' ~ '[[:cntrl:]]' as rlo, E'\u0085' ~ '[[:cntrl:]]' as c1;` Expected per the lead: rlo = false (passes), c1 = true. Then the same on the hosted project before launch.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:DB-COMMERCE-04 (impact downgraded: admin <bdi> and mail stripping verified)

doc_claims_checked.claim: PostgreSQL row locks taken by `SELECT ... ORDER BY v.id FOR UPDATE` are acquired in the sorted order (basis of the 'variants in ascending id' lock order)
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html, The Locking Clause (fetched 2026-10-07): with ORDER BY and a locking clause, ORDER BY is applied first; the command sorts the result, then may block obtaining a lock on the rows. Rows are therefore locked in sort order; the sort key here is the immutable primary key, so the documented out-of-order caveat (changed sort columns) does not apply.

findings.title: A paid Moyasar invoice that is not the store's (a dashboard invoice, a payment link, another integration on the same account) becomes an UNMAPPED_INVOICE review payment with an owner alert
findings.evidence: settlePayment fetches the payment, then its invoice, then calls applyPayment with no ownership check (payments.ts:311-323); applyPayment sends only `p_invoice: { id, status, amount, currency }` (payments.ts:291), so the invoice's metadata (order_number, attempt_id, which every store invoice carries: payments.ts:197) never reaches the SQL. apply_verified_payment step 2 (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:1007-1029) then inserts a payment_reviews row 'UNMAPPED_INVOICE' and queues finance.owner_alert('payment_review') for every charged payment whose invoice no attempt maps. A Moyasar webhook is account-wide (docs.moyasar.com/docs/api/other/webhooks/create-webhook.md: omitting events listens to all events), and the runbook registers it for 'every payment event' (docs/payments-runbook.md:297). The contract only considered another account's or a forged id (P08-CONTRACT.md:94).
findings.impact: If Anas's Moyasar account is used for anything else (an invoice created by hand in the dashboard, a payment link, another shop), every such sale becomes an open review payment on the reconciliation screen and the home's «دفعات قيد المراجعة», and every owner gets a priority-0 «تنبيه: دفعة تحتاج مراجعة» mail (counted against the 100-a-day Resend budget). The runbook presents a review payment as money that could not settle an order and that can be refunded by its own id from the admin (docs/payments-runbook.md:205), so a legitimate outside sale can be refunded by mistake. Precondition: the account is not dedicated to anas.studio.
findings.proposed_fix: In settlePayment, after fetchInvoice succeeds, close the event as 'foreign_invoice' (no apply, no review, no alert) when the fetched invoice is recognisably not the store's: it carries neither the store's metadata.attempt_id nor its callback_url (<FUNCTIONS_PUBLIC_URL>/payments/callback, which every store invoice is created with: payments.ts:192; add callback_url to the client's invoice schema). Checking the callback_url too keeps the rule safe under the dropInvoiceMetadata reading the emulator still models. Alternatively pass that flag to apply_verified_payment and let step 2 skip the review row. If the owner confirms the account is dedicated to the site, write that rule into the runbook instead.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack plus emulator: POST /v1/invoices directly at the emulator with no metadata (a dashboard invoice), then POST /__emulator/pay {invoiceId, status:'paid'} with webhookUrl set. Expected wrong result: `select reason from finance.payment_reviews where provider_invoice_id = '<id>'` returns 'UNMAPPED_INVOICE' and finance.email_outbox holds an owner_alert row whose payload alert is 'payment_review'.

findings.title: A webhook that fails the secret check (wrong Secret Token, wrong HTTP method) leaves no trace, and the webhook is the only automatic observer of dashboard refunds and voids on paid orders
findings.evidence: `if (!secretsMatch(event.secret_token, deps.config.webhookSecret)) return failWith(401, ...)` (payments.ts:435); a non-POST answers 405 (payments.ts:422) and a body without secret_token 422 (payments.ts:432); nothing in payments.ts logs (no console call in the file). Paid attempts get next_check_at null (payment_core.sql:1162-1166), and payment_check_begin and payment_callback_begin only ask about attempts that are not paid (attempt_worth_asking, payment_core.sql:500-513), so after the payment only settlePayment (the webhook) reaches apply_verified_payment step 4, which raises the external_refund and provider_status alerts (payment_core.sql:1057-1064, 515-553). Moyasar retries a non-2xx 5 more times, then drops it (webhook-reference.md), and its own page asks to 'Enable logs/alerts for payment failures and webhook failures' when switching to live (docs/getting-started/test-vs-live-environments.md). The runbook's live step (docs/payments-runbook.md:298) registers the live webhook with no check that one arrives.
findings.impact: A Secret Token mistyped when the live webhook is registered (a separate registration from the sandbox one) silently turns every live webhook into a 401. Payments still settle through the return page and the job (slower), but a refund or void made in Moyasar's dashboard on a paid order is never seen: no external_refund or provider_status alert, the order stays paid and its downloads stay granted until someone presses «أعد الفحص» (which cannot see a void either, EF-MONEY-09) or starts another refund. Nobody learns that the webhook is broken.
findings.proposed_fix: Emit one fixed-code log line (no value) on the 401, 405 and 422 paths of the webhook, e.g. console.warn('payments: webhook refused', code); add to the runbook's live step (and to the E02 record) that a finance.payment_events row must arrive for the first payment after the webhook is registered (Moyasar's GET /v1/webhooks/attempts also shows delivery results); optionally show the time of the newest payment_events row in the settings screen's payments box.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-09 (raised from low: the webhook is the only automatic path to the external_refund and provider_status alerts)

findings.title: A refused invoice creation (401, 403, 405 or 400 from Moyasar) raises no alert and keeps no HTTP status, so a wrong or regenerated live key silently turns every checkout into «تعذّر تجهيز الدفع» while the store stays open
findings.evidence: createInvoice: `if (created.kind === 'refused' || created.kind === 'not_found' || created.kind === 'rate_limited') { await closeAttempt(deps, begun.attemptId, 'failed', created.kind === 'rate_limited' ? 'CREATE_RATE_LIMITED' : 'CREATE_REFUSED'); return { state: 'unavailable' } }` (payments.ts:203-206): the HTTP status the client returns (`status` in MoyasarResult, payments/moyasar.ts:195) is dropped, and payment_attempt_close raises no alert (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:896-935). quote's checkoutEnabled is the SQL switch, seller and policies ANDed with paymentsConfig().ok and the fence (checkout.ts:322), all static checks that never ask Moyasar, so the store keeps offering checkout. The hold view shows «تعذّر تجهيز الدفع؛ حاول بعد لحظات.» (src/components/store/HoldView.tsx:250-253) and each retry makes another failed attempt until TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS (5, payment_core.sql:810). Moyasar answers 401 for an invalid key and 405 account_inactive_error for a live key on an account not activated (docs.moyasar.com/docs/api/errors.md), and tells merchants to regenerate a leaked key at once (docs/api/authentication.md), which kills the old one. tests/integration/payment-http.test.ts:832 pins the silent 'failed, unavailable' outcome.
findings.impact: A live key mistyped at go-live, or regenerated after a suspected leak without the Supabase secret being updated, makes every buyer fill the form, pass Turnstile, hold stock for 20 minutes and then read that the payment could not be prepared. No alert, no log line and no home counter tells the owner; the reconciliation screen lists only UNCERTAIN, UNVERIFIED, PROVIDER_STATUS and EXTERNAL_REFUND attempts (docs/operations.md:956). The first signal is a buyer's complaint or a launch with no sales.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the status in the code (`CREATE_REFUSED_${created.status}`) and have payment_attempt_close queue one deduplicated owner alert per day for a CREATE_REFUSED close (finance.owner_alert('payment_create_refused', current_date::text, {status})); add a live smoke test (one real low-value invoice created and cancelled) to the runbook's live step.

findings.title: Nothing handles an invoice that a declined card turns 'failed': pay keeps handing out its URL, cancel answers 409 for the rest of the hold, and the return page reads 'pending' for up to 24 hours; the emulator never produces that state
findings.evidence: Cancel closes only on `invoice.data.status === 'canceled'` or `'expired'` (checkout.ts:394-396), everything else is `refusal(first)` = 409 PAYMENT_ACTIVE «الدفع قيد المعالجة؛ حاول بعد لحظات.»; startPayment returns a pending attempt's stored URL without asking the provider (payments.ts:258, payment_core.sql:792-796); payment_attempt_checked closes a pending attempt early only for a provider status 'expired' or 'canceled' (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:1116-1120), else 24 hours after expiry; payment_view answers 'pending' while any attempt is active, whatever the order's status (20261003100000_payment_view_expiry.sql:40-51). Moyasar's invoice status list includes 'failed' (docs.moyasar.com/api/invoices/01-create-invoice) and what a failed payment does to the invoice is open sandbox item 6 (docs/payments-runbook.md:361). The emulator only ever moves an invoice to 'paid' (tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts:580-586) and keeps it payable after a failure; the only integration or e2e test that sets an invoice status through /__emulator/invoice sets 'canceled' (tests/integration/checkout-http.test.ts:589). The unit test pins the conservative choice for any status the code does not decide (tests/unit/checkout.test.ts:1296-1306: 'the invoice is on hold, or in a status nothing here decides' and 'the listed payment is not charged' answer 409 and cancel nothing), so the behaviour is deliberate; what is missing is a branch for the reading in which a declined card leaves the invoice unpayable.
findings.impact: If a declined card makes the real invoice 'failed' (and unpayable), the buyer whose card is declined, the most common payment failure, cannot pay again (the hold view's «ادفع الآن» keeps opening the dead invoice), cannot cancel (409 on every press, each spending the 30-per-hour cancel throttle) and cannot start a new order in the same session (ACTIVE_HOLD) until the 20-minute hold runs out; after that the return and order pages say 'pending' for up to a day. The suite cannot show it because the harness has no such state, and only sandbox run 3 would reveal it, with no code ready for the answer.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a fetched invoice that lists no charged payment and whose status is neither 'initiated' nor 'paid' (failed, voided, on_hold) like a canceled one in checkout's cancel and in payment_attempt_checked (close the attempt), and in startPayment close such a pending attempt and begin a new one instead of returning its URL; add an emulator switch (failedPaymentFailsInvoice) and run the cancel and pay tests under it.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack plus emulator: create an order (create), then POST /__emulator/pay {invoiceId, status:'failed'} and POST /__emulator/invoice {invoiceId, status:'failed'}. Then: `pay` answers 200 {payment:{state:'ready', url:<that invoice>}}; `cancel` answers 409 PAYMENT_ACTIVE (the emulator's cancel answers 400 'Cancel failed. The Invoice is already failed.'); after hold_expires_at, verify answers state 'pending'. Sandbox run 3 says whether the real invoice reaches 'failed'.

findings.title: The invoice callback is throttled by the caller's IP, and every callback comes from Moyasar's servers, so all buyers share one bucket of 60 per hour
findings.evidence: callback passes `p_ip_hash: await clientKeyHash(request, pepper)` (payments.ts:485); payment_callback_begin answers {} silently once `rate_limit_take('payment-callback:ip', p_ip_hash, 60, interval '1 hour')` is spent (payment_core.sql:1343-1345). The callback is a server-to-server POST from Moyasar to callback_url (docs.moyasar.com/api/invoices/01-create-invoice: an endpoint on your server that will get a POST request with the invoice object when the invoice is paid), so the IP key is Moyasar's egress address for every buyer. Provider calls per attempt are already bounded by attempt_worth_asking and the 5-second fetched_at guard (payment_core.sql:1349-1360), and an unknown invoice id never causes a fetch.
findings.impact: From the 61st paid invoice in an hour (a launch day), callbacks are dropped without a trace; settlement then waits for the webhook, the buyer's return page or the job, whose checks of a pending attempt back off 1, 2, 4 … 30 minutes. No money is lost; the prompt stops working when it is most useful.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the callback throttle on the invoice id, or drop it (the worth-asking rule and the 5-second guard already bound provider calls), or make it a store-wide ceiling far above the order rate.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-02

findings.title: The webhook settles the payment (two provider fetches of up to 10 s each) before it answers, against Moyasar's rule to return 2xx before any complex logic
findings.evidence: After payment_event_record the handler awaits settlePayment (payments.ts:462), which awaits fetchPayment and fetchInvoice, each bounded by MOYASAR_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 (payments/moyasar.ts:21), then apply_verified_payment and payment_event_result; only then it returns 200 (payments.ts:466). Moyasar: 'Your endpoint must quickly return a successful status code (2xx) before any complex logic that could cause a timeout. For example, you must return a 2xx response before updating a customer's invoice as paid' (docs.moyasar.com/docs/api/other/webhooks/webhook-reference.md, fetched 2026-10-07). The contract quotes only the first half (PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md:70) and specifies the inline settle (:407). Supabase offers EdgeRuntime.waitUntil for work after the response (supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/background-tasks).
findings.impact: When Moyasar's API or the database is slow, the reply can pass Moyasar's undocumented delivery timeout: the delivery counts as failed, is retried (answered 200 as a duplicate) and shows as failed in Moyasar's webhook attempts. Correctness holds (the event is durable first and every step is idempotent); the cost is noise and an endpoint Moyasar sees as unreliable.
findings.proposed_fix: Answer 200 right after payment_event_record and run the settle with EdgeRuntime.waitUntil (the recorded event already hands an unfinished settle to the job 30 s later), or leave it to the job; amend contract section 7 accordingly.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-01

findings.title: The runbook says the emulator accepts a past expired_at and expires the invoice at once; the emulator refuses it with 400
findings.evidence: docs/payments-runbook.md:155: 'An invoice that has `expired_at` in the past at creation is accepted and is `expired` at once.' The emulator answers 400 validation_error (tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts:664-667: `else if (typeof expiredAt === 'string' && Date.parse(expiredAt) < Date.now()) errors.expired_at = [...]`), aligned in commit ced46d4 to the sandbox answer the same runbook records at line 55 ('a past time is refused (400)').
findings.impact: The 'harness choices' list is the one place that says where the emulator departs from documented behaviour, and it is wrong here: a late-payment or expiry test written from it expects 201 and gets 400.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the bullet: a past expired_at answers 400 validation_error, as the sandbox does; an invoice expires when its expired_at passes (a test sets an earlier time with /__emulator/invoice).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-03

findings.title: Contract section 9 still describes the pre-sandbox emulator: a cancel of a canceled invoice answers 200 again, and the 400 body is invalid_request_error 'Validation Failed'
findings.evidence: PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md:464: 'PUT /v1/invoices/:id/cancel (an initiated invoice becomes canceled; a canceled one answers 200 again; ...)' and :467: 'Errors use the documented bodies: 400 {type:'invalid_request_error', message:'Validation Failed', errors:{field:[…]}}'. findings.title: The emulator's default accepts a further refund of a payment it has already set to 'refunded', while Moyasar's docs allow a refund only from paid or captured and say a partial refund sets 'refunded'
findings.evidence: DEFAULTS `refuseSecondRefund: false, partialRefundKeepsPaid: false` (moyasar-emulator.ts:219-220): a partial refund sets status 'refunded' (:753) and a further refund of a 'refunded' payment is accepted (:744-747). docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/payment-operations/index.md (fetched 2026-10-07): Quick Reference 'Refund … Allowed From Status: paid, captured', and under Partial Refund 'The payment status changes to `refunded`'. Only refunds-http.test.ts:587-603 and two unit tests switch refuseSecondRefund on; every other refund test and e2e runs on the permissive default.
findings.impact: The admin offers several partial refunds of one payment (a return of one item, then another). If the live API refuses a refund of a payment already 'refunded', the second partial refund fails (the ledger handles it: a 4xx is 'failed', nothing moved) and the owner has no in-admin way to return the rest. The suite, the e2e journeys and the runbook's description (docs/payments-runbook.md:92) present the permissive reading as the normal one, so this surfaces only at sandbox run 6.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the documented reading the default (refuseSecondRefund true, a partial refund setting 'refunded') and keep the permissive one as the switch; say in the refund screen's help and in the runbook that a second partial refund may be refused until sandbox item 8 is answered.
findings.proof_recipe: Sandbox run 6 (docs/payments-runbook.md): refund part of a paid test payment, then part again; record whether the second POST /payments/:id/refund answers 200 or 400 and the payment's status after the first.

findings.title: The owner's «أعد الفحص» on a paid attempt cannot see a void: settleInvoice fetches only paid, refunded and captured payments, so a voided paying payment keeps Moyasar's last status 'paid' in the order view
findings.evidence: settleInvoice: `for (const listed of invoice.data.payments) { if (!CHARGED.has(listed.status)) continue` with CHARGED = {'paid','refunded','captured'} (payments.ts:50, 358-363). paymentRecheck calls settleInvoice for any attempt with an invoice id, paid ones included (admin.ts:518-519). Step 4 of apply_verified_payment, which writes provider_status and raises the provider_status alert through finance.attempt_provider_alerts, is reached only for a fetched payment (payment_core.sql:1057-1064, 515-553); a 'voided' payment is never fetched, the invoice reads 'voided' (not paid or refunded, so no INVOICE_PAID_UNSETTLED) and payment_attempt_checked returns at once for a paid attempt (20261002145000_order_operations.sql:1091-1093). Moyasar: voided 'when the merchant cancels a paid, authorized, or captured payment', within about 2 hours of a paid one (docs/api/payments/payment-status-reference.md, docs/guides/payment-operations/index.md). operations.md:956 tells the owner «أعد الفحص» 'asks Moyasar now'.
findings.impact: After a void made in the dashboard (by Anas or anyone with dashboard access) whose payment_voided webhook was missed or never sent, the owner's recheck answers «الحالة الآن: …» with the attempt still paid and the order view keeps showing Moyasar's status as paid, so a signed or paper edition can be shipped and downloads stay granted for money that was returned. The webhook path does see voids (settlePayment applies whatever status it fetched); this is the fallback that does not.
findings.proposed_fix: In settleInvoice fetch and apply 'voided' payments as well (a separate set from CHARGED, which also drives the cancel rule): apply_verified_payment step 4 then records the status and alerts for the attempt's own payment, and step 6 answers not_paid for anyone else's.
findings.prior_overlap: earlier partial attempt of this slice (attempt-1006b EF-MONEY-01, unpublished)

findings.title: payments_kick gives pg_net 15 s while a reconciliation run is budgeted 60 s plus one row; whether the run survives the disconnect is unproven
findings.evidence: `perform net.http_post(url := v_url || '/outbox', ..., timeout_milliseconds := 15000)` (payment_core.sql:1667-1672, comment '15 s: a cold function start can exceed pg_net's 5 s default'). runPaymentsReconcile keeps taking rows for RUN_BUDGET_MS = 60_000 (payments.ts:48, 680), and the row in progress can add a cancel, an invoice fetch and one fetch per charged payment at up to 10 s each (payments/moyasar.ts:21). Supabase documents a 150 s (free) or 400 s (paid) wall clock and a 150 s request idle timeout (supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/limits) but nothing about a client that disconnects.
findings.impact: If the Edge runtime ends the handler when pg_net hangs up, every run longer than 15 s (a slow provider, precisely when reconciliation matters) stops mid-way without job_run_record, so finance.job_runs, which operations.md:1144-1150 tells the owner to read when something sticks, shows the last good run; the rows themselves keep a 2-minute lease and are retried, so no money state is lost. If the runtime keeps running, pg_net only records timeouts. The 60 s budget's premise ('outlive the function') does not match the 15 s caller.
findings.proposed_fix: Either raise payments_kick's timeout_milliseconds above the budget (about 90 000) or lower RUN_BUDGET_MS below 15 s minus a cold start; settle which with the hosted check at P11.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-08
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted project at P11: make the provider slow (a test project pointed at a URL that delays 20 s), mark one attempt due, let payments_kick fire, then `select status, finished_at from finance.job_runs where job='payments_reconcile' order by finished_at desc limit 1` and read the function logs; a missing run row for that minute while net._http_response shows a timeout proves the cut.

findings.title: A refund Moyasar refuses is recorded as «لم يتم» REFUND_REFUSED with no HTTP status, and nothing tells the owner the documented reasons (an aggregation account's balance, a payment already 'refunded')
findings.evidence: refundAtProvider maps every 4xx but 404 to `p_error: 'REFUND_REFUSED'` (refunds.ts:180-182); the client never reads the error body (payments/moyasar.ts:344-345) and the status it returns (`status` in MoyasarResult) is dropped here. The admin shows a failed refund as «لم يتم» (src/lib/admin-orders.ts:82-87). docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/payment-operations/index.md (fetched 2026-10-07): 'For live accounts using aggregation, your account balance must be sufficient to cover the refund', refunds are allowed only from paid or captured, and 'If it fails again, contact Moyasar support with the payment ID'. docs/payments-runbook.md:236 says only 'A 4xx is failed: nothing moved and the balance is free again'; settlements (twice a week) empty an aggregation account's balance (artifacts/acceptance/P08/moyasar-docs-2026-10-02.md:50).
findings.impact: Live, a refund right after a settlement payout, or a second partial refund of a payment Moyasar already marks 'refunded' (EF-MONEY-07), fails with no reason the owner can act on; he retries with a new key (another failed row each time) or gives up, while the buyer waits for money that was promised. No money moves wrongly: a 4xx is correctly 'failed'.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the status in the code (`REFUND_REFUSED_${result.status}`, still an ASCII code under the contract's rule) and add to the runbook's refund section and the refund screen's failure note the documented causes: insufficient balance on an aggregation account (wait for incoming payments or top up), a payment already fully or partially refunded, and Moyasar support with the payment id.

findings.title: The return page's verify answers an order's payment state to anyone who knows its 8-character number, with no token
findings.evidence: `const tokenHash = accessToken ? await orderAccessTokenHash(pepper, accessToken) : ZERO_HASH` (payments.ts:526), then payment_check_begin and payment_state; finance.payment_view computes state from the order alone and gates only invoiceUrl on the token (20261003100000_payment_view_expiry.sql:40-60). Throttle 120 per hour per IP hash. Contract section 6 (payment_check_begin) specifies it so the return page works when the tab lost its stored order.
findings.impact: Whoever holds an order number (it is in the success_url query string, on the receipt and in support mail) learns whether the order is paid, pending, expired, cancelled, refunded or under review, and whether the site is in test mode. No money and no personal data; a deliberate trade-off, recorded so it is not rediscovered.
findings.proposed_fix: None required. If the trade-off is revisited, answer 'unknown' without a matching token except while the order's own checkout session is the caller's.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-11

findings.title: The emulator is stricter than the sandbox on invoice metadata: it refuses a non-string value (400) and answers {} where the sandbox answers null
findings.evidence: metadataProblem: `if (typeof item !== 'string' || item.length > 500) return 'values must be strings of at most 500 characters'` (moyasar-emulator.ts:296) answers 400; createInvoice stores `{}` when no metadata was sent (:688). The sandbox record (artifacts/acceptance/P08/moyasar-sandbox-2026-10-02.md:79): 'An invoice made without metadata answers `metadata: null`. A numeric metadata value is kept as a number.' The client accepts both (`metadata: z.record(...).nullish()` and string values only, payments/moyasar.ts:243, 276).
findings.impact: Nothing today: the code sends two string values and reads null or {} alike. A later test that relies on the emulator refusing a numeric value, or on {}, passes locally and differs live.
findings.proposed_fix: Align the emulator with the sandbox (keep non-string values, answer null when none was sent) or note the difference in the runbook's harness-choices list.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-06

findings.title: The emulator caps a refund of a captured payment at its amount; Moyasar caps it at the captured amount
findings.evidence: refundPayment: `if (payment.refunded + (amount as number) > payment.amount) return invalid(...)` for paid, captured and refunded payments alike (moyasar-emulator.ts:744-748). docs.moyasar.com/docs/guides/payment-operations/index.md (fetched 2026-10-07): 'For `captured` payments, the maximum refundable amount is the `captured` amount.' A captured payment reaches the ledger only as a review payment (apply_verified_payment UNEXPECTED_STATUS) whose amount_halalas is the payment's amount, and refund_request bounds EXCEEDS_BALANCE by it (20261002130000_refunds.sql:412, 442).
findings.impact: A refund of a partially captured review payment for more than its captured amount passes the ledger and the emulator and would be refused 400 live (refund_result 'failed', nothing moved): safe, but no test can show it. Hosted invoices are not expected to produce captured payments.
findings.proposed_fix: Cap at `captured` for a captured payment in the emulator; optionally store the captured amount on the review row and bound the review refund by it.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-MONEY-07

plan_gaps.title: An operator signal for the two silent payment failures: a refused webhook and a refused invoice creation
plan_gaps.why_needed: A webhook refused for its secret or method (401, 405, 422) and an invoice creation refused by Moyasar (401, 403, 405, 400) leave no log line and raise no alert (EF-MONEY-02, EF-MONEY-08). The webhook is the only automatic observer of dashboard refunds and voids on paid orders, and a refused creation breaks every checkout while the store stays open. Moyasar's own go-live page asks for logs and alerts on payment and webhook failures, and its API exposes webhook delivery attempts (GET /v1/webhooks/attempts). The runbook's live step has no check that a live webhook arrives or that a live invoice can be created.
plan_gaps.touches: supabase/functions/_shared/payments.ts (webhook 401/405/422 log line; CREATE_REFUSED_<status>), supabase/migrations (payment_attempt_close alert), docs/payments-runbook.md live step (smoke test: one low-value live invoice created and cancelled, one payment_events row after the first live payment), optionally the settings screen's payments box (newest payment_events time)

plan_gaps.title: A rotation procedure for MOYASAR_SECRET_KEY and MOYASAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET
plan_gaps.why_needed: Moyasar tells merchants to regenerate a leaked key at once (docs/api/authentication.md), which kills the old key: from then every create is refused (silent, EF-MONEY-08) and every fetch fails until the Supabase secret is replaced. A webhook secret changed on one side only makes every delivery 401 (silent, EF-MONEY-02) and Moyasar drops each event after about 3 h 41 min of retries. The runbook says only that a lost key is regenerated (docs/payments-runbook.md:325): no order of steps, no window, no check afterwards.
plan_gaps.touches: docs/payments-runbook.md, docs/operations.md

plan_gaps.title: Decide whether the Moyasar account is dedicated to anas.studio, or make the webhook ignore invoices the store did not create
plan_gaps.why_needed: Every charged payment on an invoice no attempt maps becomes an UNMAPPED_INVOICE review payment with an owner alert (EF-MONEY-01). Dashboard invoices, payment links or another shop on the same account would fill the review list with legitimate sales that the runbook presents as refundable money in review.
plan_gaps.touches: supabase/functions/_shared/payments.ts settlePayment (or apply_verified_payment step 2), docs/payments-runbook.md

plan_gaps.title: Code and emulator readiness for the other answer to sandbox item 6 (a failed payment fails the invoice)
plan_gaps.why_needed: Every other open sandbox question has an emulator switch and code that handles both readings; item 6 has neither. If the real invoice turns 'failed' after a declined card, the buyer can neither pay again nor cancel for the rest of the hold, and the return page reads 'pending' for up to a day (EF-MONEY-12). Preparing the branch before E02 run 3 avoids a new build round at the last gate.
plan_gaps.touches: tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts (switch), supabase/functions/_shared/checkout.ts cancel, supabase/functions/_shared/payments.ts startPayment, payment_attempt_checked

plan_gaps.title: Hosted check: does a reconciliation run survive pg_net's 15 s timeout?
plan_gaps.why_needed: payments_kick gives pg_net 15 s; runPaymentsReconcile is budgeted 60 s plus one row (EF-MONEY-10). Supabase documents the wall clock but not what happens to a handler whose client disconnects. Either the budget or the timeout must change, and only the hosted runtime can say which.
