findings.title: The accepted contact:all residual rests on a fallback e-mail that no page publishes
findings.evidence: docs/operations.md:167-171: 'an attacker who passes Turnstile can spend the whole 40/day budget ... and lock the form for everyone else until the next UTC midnight; real visitors get «أرسلت رسائل كثيرة؛ حاول لاحقًا.» and still have the published email address (`help@anas.studio`)'. ripgrep over src/ and content/ finds no help@anas.studio, no mailto: and no render of site_settings contact.email (only the admin field src/admin/collections/site-settings.ts:74); PLANS/ISSUES.md I45(3) says the same: «بريد التواصل» 'is validated and published, but no page shows it'.
findings.impact: The risk acceptance for a global 40-a-day contact cap that any Turnstile-solving attacker can spend is justified by a fallback channel that does not exist on the built site. When the form is locked, a real visitor (a publisher, a client for a session) has no published e-mail and is told he himself sent too many messages; the owner believes such visitors can still write.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the residual paragraph in docs/operations.md: say that no e-mail is published today (I45(3)) and that the visitors' only alternative while the form is locked is the social tiles (when I41's bootstrap has put them on /contact); or, if Anas decides under I45(3) to show the address, publish it on /contact and keep the sentence.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-06 (confirmed; placed here at the document whose premise is false); I45(3) records that no page shows the contact e-mail

findings.title: The 60-second file link is only a token expiry: on Supabase Pro the Smart CDN keeps serving a fetched signed URL after it expires and after a refund
findings.evidence: download.ts:37-38 `/** How long a file link lives. */ const SIGNED_SECONDS = 60`, and the header (lines 18-20) promises a link 'never once the entitlement is revoked or the order refunded'. The paid file is uploaded by src/components/admin/VariantCommerce.tsx:205 `uploadToSignedUrl(signed.path, signed.token, body, { contentType: checked.mime })` with no cacheControl, so storage-js 2.117.1 (dist/index.mjs:598-599, 770) stores `cacheControl: "3600"`. docs/costs.md:21 puts live orders on Supabase Pro. Supabase's Smart CDN page (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/cdn/smart-cdn, fetched 2026-10-07): 'Smart CDN caching is automatically enabled for Pro Plan and above', 'the asset is cached on the CDN for as long as possible', 'Revoking or expiring a token does not purge its CDN cache entry', 'that cached response can continue to be served for the same signed URL until the CDN cache duration expires, even if the token in that URL has already expired. If you need to cut off access to an asset, delete the object'.
findings.impact: Once a buyer (or anyone holding the URL) fetches a signed file link, that exact URL keeps returning the paid PDF/EPUB from the edge it was cached at, long after 60 seconds and after the order is refunded and the entitlement revoked. A buyer can post the link and it keeps working for others served by that edge; the per-token use count and the 10-a-day issue cap (which count signatures, not fetches) no longer bound distribution, and the refund revocation the contract promises does not reach a cached link.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the behaviour to the I32 hosted checks and settle it on the Pro project before live orders: fetch one signed paid-file URL, wait past 60 s, fetch it again and read `cf-cache-status`. If it is a HIT, either upload paid files with a zero cache lifetime and re-check, or serve the bytes through the download function instead of a CDN-cached Storage URL; otherwise record the residual in docs/operations.md and contract section 7 (the link is a bearer link of at least 60 s, not a revocable one).
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted Pro project with a real paid file: POST /functions/v1/download {action:'issue',...} then {action:'redeem',downloadToken} to get url U. curl -sI U (expect 200, note cf-cache-status MISS). Wait 90 s. curl -sI U again. Wrong result: 200 with cf-cache-status: HIT (a 400/403 means the token expiry holds). Repeat after refunding the order: a 200 HIT is the revocation leak.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-07 (extended with the Supabase Smart CDN documentation); I32 lists Range and nosniff on the signed file reply as hosted checks, not CDN caching

findings.title: The launch plan attaches www.anas.studio to the Pages site, but every public function accepts exactly one origin and one Turnstile hostname
findings.evidence: WORK-PACKAGES.md:143 (and SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md:49): 'take anas.studio and www off the Worker anas-studio-soon and attach them to the Pages project'; no redirect of www to the apex is planned anywhere in PLANS/ or docs/. The functions compare the request's Origin with the single SITE_URL origin: http.ts:38-46 `siteOrigin()` returns `new URL(siteUrl).origin`; contact.ts:98, notify.ts:105, orders.ts:147 and download.ts:114 answer 403 `FORBIDDEN` «طلب غير مسموح.» when `request.headers.get('origin') !== allowed`, and send ACAO for the apex only; Turnstile is checked against `new URL(siteUrl).hostname` (contact.ts:134, notify.ts:143, orders.ts:191). Cloudflare documents the www case for Pages as a Bulk Redirect (www -> apex, 301, path and query kept) plus a proxied placeholder record, not as a second custom domain on the project (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/how-to/www-redirect/index.md, updated Apr 21, 2026).
findings.impact: A visitor who opens https://www.anas.studio (typed, or from a link that uses www) gets a fully rendered site on which every server action fails: the contact form, the availability sign-up, the order page and its recovery, downloads and checkout all answer 403 (the browser also refuses to read the reply, so the pages show their network sentence). Nothing in the P11 proof list exercises a form on www.
findings.proposed_fix: In P11, attach www only as a redirect: a Cloudflare redirect rule (or Bulk Redirect) sending https://www.anas.studio/* to https://anas.studio/$1 with the path, query and status 301, and add to the launch smoke a contact or notify call made from a page loaded on www that must arrive on the apex. Do not widen the functions' origin check.
findings.proof_recipe: After the P11 domain step: curl -sI https://www.anas.studio/contact must answer 301 with location https://anas.studio/contact. Wrong result: 200 (the site served on www), after which a contact submit from that page answers 403 FORBIDDEN.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-02 (same finding, confirmed); no ISSUES or round entry

findings.title: After a pepper change, link recovery renews the dead stored hash instead of replacing it, so a buyer who keeps recovering is locked out of his order
findings.evidence: orders.ts:95 `if (!order.expired) return { orderId: order.orderId, version: order.tokenVersion }` sends no hash for an unexpired token; delivery.sql:234-238 then only renews it: `set access_token_expires_at = now() + interval '7 days' ... where o.id = r.order_id and o.access_token_version = r.version and o.access_token_expires_at > now()`, and queues an `order_link` mail whose token the dispatcher derives with the CURRENT pepper (outbox.ts:177 `orderAccessToken(pepper, data.idempotencyKey, data.tokenVersion)`). Nothing checks that the stored `access_token_hash` is the current pepper's hash of that token. docs/operations.md:1383-1389 tells the operator a new pepper 'makes every stored order link ... stop matching (404)' and recovery is the buyer's way back (the order page's 404 shows the recovery form).
findings.impact: Precondition: TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER is replaced (lost in a disaster restore, or rotated after a suspected leak). Every buyer whose link has not expired (paid, renewed or filed within 7 days) gets 404 on the order page, asks for a new link, and receives one derived from the new pepper that matches nothing; each request renews the old hash for another 7 days, so a buyer who keeps trying never gets in, cannot download a paid file and cannot file a return until he stops for a full week.
findings.proposed_fix: Let recovery prove the stored token before renewing it: have recoveryItems send the current version's hash for an unexpired order too, and in order_recover_apply renew only when `access_token_hash = r.current_hash`; otherwise treat the order as expired and set the next version's hash (the existing expired branch). Add a line to the restore runbook that a new pepper needs this path.
findings.prior_overlap: none: the runbook records that a new pepper kills mailed links, not that recovery cannot repair them

findings.title: A confirmation mail the backlog queues late dies before its promised 7 days: the purge ages pending rows by updated_at, which queueing never moves
findings.evidence: notify_confirm_queue (line 124) records the mail with `update public.notifications n set confirm_sent_at = now() where n.id = p_id` and leaves updated_at; no trigger maintains notifications.updated_at (payment_core.sql:380-402 has none). notifications_purge (line 423) deletes `n.status = 'pending' and n.updated_at < now() - interval '7 days'`. notify_confirm_backlog (hourly, lines 136-161) queues rows a cap held back hours or days after the sign-up; notify.ts:174 honours a link while `Date.now() - row.confirmSentAt <= 7 days` and email.ts:508 tells the visitor «وهو صالح لمدة 7 أيام».
findings.impact: A visitor who signs up for a second variant the same UTC day (the address cap holds the mail to the next day's backlog), or any sign-up held behind a spent day's 30, gets a confirmation link the 03:37 purge deletes at sign-up + 7 days, one or more days before the 7 days the mail states; on a flooded week a mail can arrive with hours left or after its row is gone, and pressing «تأكيد» then says «الرابط غير صالح أو انتهت صلاحيته.».
findings.proposed_fix: Set updated_at = now() together with confirm_sent_at in finance.notify_confirm_queue (the row's last activity is the mail), or purge pending rows by greatest(updated_at, coalesce(confirm_sent_at, updated_at)); add the case to tests/integration/notify.test.ts.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-01; round-08 recorded only the queued-versus-sent clock, not the purge clock

findings.title: Link recovery only ever lists an address's five newest orders and the admin cannot resend a link, so an older order's page and paid file become unreachable for good
findings.evidence: order_recover_list selects `... and o.status in ('paid', 'paid_needs_resolution', 'refunded') order by o.created_at desc, o.id desc limit 5` (lines 190-196); order_recover_apply refuses more than 5 items (line 225). Every token expires 7 days after payment, reissue or file attach (P08-CONTRACT line 170), and order_access/download_issue/return_request_create refuse an expired one (lines 94, 301, 542). The only `order_link` producer is order_recover_apply (grep of supabase/migrations for 'order_link' inserts: delivery.sql:253 only); admin.ts and src/components/admin have no resend action. Refunded orders also take slots in the five.
findings.impact: A returning reader with six or more paid or refunded orders on one address who comes back after 7 days for an older purchase (the digital edition bought months ago, a return on an older shipment) asks for links and receives the five newest only; the older order's page, its download and its return form can never be reached again, and Anas has no tool to send the link.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the owner a 'send the order link again' action on the admin order view (owner, audited): it bumps the version when the token is expired (the recover_apply rule) and queues one `order_link` for that order under the existing per-order daily key. Optionally rank recovery by expired orders with a live entitlement first.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-03

findings.title: Shipping and refund mails carry the personal order link without renewing its 7-day life, so a preorder's shipment or a late refund mails a dead link
findings.evidence: The token's expiry is set to now()+7 days at payment (payment_core.sql:1143) and renewed only by recovery (delivery.sql:236, 242), paid_asset_set (delivery.sql:458-460) and order_resolve (order_operations.sql:967): exactly the list of P08-CONTRACT line 170. fulfillment_update queues `order_shipped` (order_operations.sql:721-724) and the refund paths queue `order_refunded` (refunds.sql:248-250, stats_disputes.sql:212-214) without touching access_token_expires_at. The dispatcher puts the link in every such mail (email.ts:371-372 «صفحة طلبك (الرابط شخصي، لا تشاركه):» + `${siteUrl}/orders#...`), derived from the current version (outbox.ts:177) with no expiry check.
findings.impact: Every physical or signed preorder ships after its date, often weeks after payment, and so does any order shipped or refunded more than 7 days after payment: the buyer's «شُحن» or refund mail invites him to his order page and the link answers «لم نجد هذا الطلب، أو انتهت صلاحية رابطه.»; the return form he would use after delivery is behind the same dead link, so every such buyer must go through recovery (Turnstile, a second mail, the 20-a-day cap and the five-order limit of EF-ACCESS-06).
findings.proposed_fix: Where fulfillment_update queues order_shipped and where the refund success paths queue order_refunded, also renew the token like paid_asset_set does: `update finance.orders set access_token_expires_at = greatest(access_token_expires_at, now() + interval '7 days') where id = <order>` (renewing an expired one revives the current version, as paid_asset_set already does), and add the two kinds to contract line 170.
findings.prior_overlap: an earlier cut-off attempt of this slice noted it (scratch only); not in the leads, ISSUES or round audits; the docs/operations.md residual 'a link mailed more than 7 days late is dead' covers delayed mail, not a shipment or refund that legitimately comes more than 7 days after payment

findings.title: TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER is accepted at any non-empty length, though it is the only secret behind every buyer and subscriber token
findings.evidence: optionalEnv (env.ts:122-125) refuses only an empty value; orders.ts:136, download.ts:103, notify.ts:94 and contact.ts:141 accept whatever it returns. tokens.ts:43-45 derives the order token as HMAC(pepper, 'order-access:' + idempotencyKey) and stores sha256(`${pepper}:order:${token}`); tokens.ts:61-62 derives the notify token as HMAC(pepper, 'notify:' + id + ':' + version). paymentsConfig refuses a webhook secret under 32 characters (moyasar.ts:90) but nothing sizes the pepper, and .env.example:27-32 and docs/operations.md step 5 give no length or generation command.
findings.impact: Precondition: the operator sets a short or memorable pepper. A buyer holding his own idempotency key (sessionStorage) and token can test candidate peppers offline; anyone who also reads the database (a leaked backup, a staff session reading public.notifications, the owner's export) can then mint a working link for every order (downloads of paid files, return requests) and every subscription, which a strong pepper prevents even with the database in hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Refuse a pepper shorter than 32 characters where it is read (one helper used by the five functions, answering 503 like a missing one), and write `openssl rand -base64 32` beside TOKEN_HASH_PEPPER in .env.example and the P11 secrets step.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-04

findings.title: The contact form's 5,500-byte message check ignores JSON escaping and the other fields, so a message it accepts can still exceed the function's 8 KiB body
findings.evidence: ContactForm.tsx:18 `MESSAGE_MAX_BYTES = 5500` and line 92 measure only `new TextEncoder().encode(values.message.trim()).length`; the body (lines 110-117) also carries name (maxLength 120 UTF-16 units, up to 360 bytes), email (254), submissionKey (36), turnstileToken (the schema and Cloudflare allow 2048 characters: contact.ts:82, developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/server-side-validation/ 'Maximum length: 2048 characters') and about 110 bytes of keys, and JSON.stringify writes every line break as two bytes. contact.ts:32 refuses anything over 8,192 bytes with 413 «رسالتك أطول من المسموح؛ اختصرها وأرسلها من جديد.». With a 2,048-character token, an Arabic name and a short address, a 5,500-byte message with more than about 260 line breaks (a poem) is refused.
findings.impact: A visitor whose message passed the form's own check is told after pressing «أرسل» that it is too long, and has to cut text the form said fitted; the 413 comes before siteverify, so only the widget reset costs him (the form resets Turnstile in `finally`). Rare: a near-limit message with many lines or a long challenge token.
findings.proposed_fix: Check the size of the JSON body the form is about to send (`new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(body)).length <= 8192`) instead of the message alone, keeping the message-field error copy.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-05 (corrected: the token is not spent by a 413, and a 120-unit name is at most 360 bytes); AUDIT-1 S16.1 holds only partly

findings.title: A return request carries no idempotency key, so a retry after a lost reply files a second request
findings.evidence: ReturnForm posts `{action:'return-request', orderNumber, accessToken, items: chosen, reason: why}` (OrderPage.tsx:214-220) and on a network failure keeps the quantities and reason and re-enables the button (lines 233-236); returnSchema (orders.ts:66-71) has no key and return_request_create inserts a new row for every accepted call (delivery.sql:598-600), refusing a repeat only when the summed quantities exceed finance.item_returnable (lines 588-594) or the 5-a-day cap is reached.
findings.impact: A buyer on a weak mobile connection whose first press was stored but whose reply was lost presses again: if he asked for fewer units than he may return, a second identical request is filed and the staff see two open returns for one parcel; if he asked for all of them, he is told «تحقق من المنتجات والكميات المطلوب إرجاعها.» although his request went through.
findings.proposed_fix: Mint a request key in ReturnForm (kept until the form changes, like ContactForm's submissionKey), send it as `requestKey`, store it in finance.return_requests with a unique constraint and answer the existing returnId for a repeat.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-08

findings.title: Observation: the per-IP throttle key is salted with the UTC date, so every hourly per-IP window starts again at UTC midnight
findings.evidence: clientKeyHash hashes `${pepper}:${utcDate}:${throttleAddress(requestIp(request))}` (rate-limit.ts:130-136); finance.rate_limit_take keys the window on (bucket, key_hash, window_start). A caller at 23:59 and 00:01 UTC has two key_hash values, so contact:ip (5), notify:ip (5), order-recover:ip (10) and the 120-an-hour buyer buckets allow a second full window across midnight (03:00 Riyadh).
findings.impact: At most a doubled per-IP allowance once a day for a caller who times it; the email-keyed and global buckets carry no date. A deliberate unlinkability trade-off (the module's header), recorded because docs/operations.md states the limits as plain hourly numbers.
findings.proposed_fix: None needed; optionally say in docs/operations.md that per-IP windows also reset at 00:00 UTC.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ACCESS-09

findings.title: A missing or malformed Moyasar setting takes down every buyer's order page, downloads, returns and link recovery, and the runbook does not say so
findings.evidence: download.ts:134-135 and orders.ts:166-167: `const config = deps.config ?? paymentsConfig(); if (!config.ok) return fail(503, 'UNAVAILABLE', FAILED)` before any database call, for get, recover, return-request, issue and redeem alike. These actions use only `config.mode` and `config.storageBase`, but paymentsConfig (moyasar.ts:75-127) is not ok whenever any of the five Moyasar variables is absent, the key prefix does not match the mode, the webhook secret is under 32 characters, or a base ends with a slash. docs/payments-runbook.md:292 lists what stops 'While paymentsConfig() is not ok' (quote, create, webhook, callback, verify, the switch, the job) and omits the order page, recovery, returns and downloads.
findings.impact: During a key rotation with a typo, a too-short new webhook secret, the sandbox-to-live switch done one secret at a time, or after the owner removes the Moyasar keys because the store is closed, every buyer who already paid sees «تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة؛ أعد المحاولة.» on his order page and cannot download the book he bought, file a return or recover his link, for as long as the payment settings stay wrong; the operator, following the runbook, expects only new purchases to stop.
findings.proposed_fix: Give orders and download their own small check that reads only PAYMENTS_MODE (test or live) and FUNCTIONS_PUBLIC_URL (for the Storage base), refusing with 503 only when those two are unusable; at minimum add the four buyer actions to the runbook's list of what a bad payment setting stops.
findings.prior_overlap: none: the contract states 'without payments there are no orders' for a never-configured project, not the post-sale outage

findings.title: A leaked order link can be kept alive indefinitely through recovery, and neither the buyer nor the owner can revoke it
findings.evidence: For an unexpired token, order_recover_apply only renews it: `set access_token_expires_at = now() + interval '7 days' ... where o.access_token_version = r.version and o.access_token_expires_at > now()` (lines 234-238); a new version is minted only once the old token has expired (lines 239-244, orders.ts:95-101). Recovery is open to anyone who knows the address (Turnstile, 3 an hour per address). No owner action or SQL function rotates a live token (grep of admin.ts and the migrations: access_token_hash is written only by checkout_create and order_recover_apply). The link reaches places outside the buyer's control: a forwarded receipt, the browser's global history (takeFragment's replaceState, src/lib/orders.ts:65-74, changes only the current entry), mail link scanners, and Resend's 30-day log (docs/privacy-data-map.md:33).
findings.impact: Whoever holds a leaked link and the buyer's address (both visible in a forwarded receipt) can keep the order page alive for good by asking for recovery every few days: he keeps downloading the paid file (10 tokens a day), sees the tracking numbers and can file return requests, while each renewal mails the real buyer a link he did not ask for. A buyer who notices cannot end it, and the owner has no way to rotate that order's link.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an owner action that rotates one order's link (bump access_token_version, store the new version's hash derived in the admin function, mail order_link): the same tool EF-ACCESS-06 needs. Optionally stop recovery from extending a token that recovery already renewed in the last 7 days.
findings.prior_overlap: none: round 7 accepted 'recovery never kills a working link' to stop strangers killing links; the inverse (a leaked link cannot be killed) is not recorded

findings.title: Any script can spend the project's Edge Function invocation quota with refused requests, and any buyer its Storage egress: no control runs before the metered resource
findings.evidence: contact, notify, orders and download (and checkout, payments) run with verify_jwt = false (supabase/config.toml:417-445) and their own first checks are the method and the Origin header (contact.ts:94-98, notify.ts:101-105, orders.ts:143-147, download.ts:110-114); every throttle sits in SQL after that. Supabase bills 'the number of times your functions get invoked, regardless of the response status code. Preflight (OPTIONS) requests are not billed' (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/edge-function-invocations.md, fetched 2026-10-07). docs/costs.md:12 puts the launch on the Free plan with 500,000 invocations; the Fair Use Policy (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/billing-faq.md) restricts an organization that keeps exceeding it: 'Pausing projects', 'Switching databases to read-only mode', 'Responding with a 402 status code for all API requests', lifted at the next billing cycle; https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/limits.md documents no per-caller rate limit. Neither docs/operations.md's 'Residuals and ceilings (accepted)' (line 1154) nor costs.md records the risk or a response.
findings.impact: Someone with a loop of `curl -X POST <functions>/contact` (no Turnstile, no Origin needed to be billed) passes 500,000 invocations in a few hours for nothing. After the grace period the whole organization can be restricted: every Supabase API call answers 402, so the admin, staff sign-in, the contact form, availability sign-ups, the order pages and the site-state gate's read fail until the next billing cycle or an upgrade. On Pro with the spend cap on (the default) the same happens past 2 million; with it off the attacker sets the bill at $2 per million. The same holds for Storage egress: a signed paid-file URL allows unlimited GETs while valid and, cached by the Smart CDN, after it (EF-ACCESS-02); Pro has 250 GB uncached / 250 GB cached egress, then $0.09/$0.03 per GB or Fair Use restrictions with the spend cap on (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/egress.md), and download_redeem's 3 uses and 10 tokens a day count signatures, not bytes, so one purchase lets a script drain it.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide and record before launch, as an accepted residual with a response: a usage alert on invocations and egress (P10 monitoring) and a runbook step for a flood (upgrade, or turn the spend cap off for the rest of the cycle and accept $2 per million invocations). A Cloudflare front for /functions/v1 would not remove the risk, because the project's own <ref>.supabase.co function and Storage URLs stay public and billable.
findings.prior_overlap: none: costs.md lists the quotas; no audit or ISSUES entry treats them as abuse budgets

findings.title: Staff sign-in codes can be requested by anyone with no CAPTCHA: a script drains the project's Auth mail cap and the shared Resend quota
findings.evidence: SignIn calls `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: false } })` with no captchaToken; supabase/config.toml leaves `# [auth.captcha]` commented out and I28's hosted checklist does not add CAPTCHA. Supabase limits (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits): one OTP per user per 60 s, emails sent are a per-project limit, and with custom SMTP the default is 30 messages per hour (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp). The sign-in mails go out through the same Resend account as receipts (docs/operations.md 'Sign-in codes share the account but are not counted'); Resend Free allows 100 per day and 3,000 per month (https://resend.com/pricing). POST /auth/v1/recover (default English recovery template) is a second unauthenticated mail trigger for the same addresses.
findings.impact: Anyone who knows one staff address (the publishable key ships in every page) can request a code every 61 s: Anas's inbox gets about 30 codes an hour, the project's 30-per-hour Auth mail cap is used up so a real staff member asking for a code gets 429 «أُرسلت رموز كثيرة…» and cannot sign in on a new device, and after about 3.3 hours Resend's 100-per-day quota is gone, so every outbox mail (receipts, download-ready, shipping, refund notices, contact notices) waits for the next UTC day, every day the script runs. The docs' 20-send reserve 'for sign-in codes' assumes sign-in volume is legitimate and low.
findings.proposed_fix: Turn on Supabase Auth CAPTCHA with Cloudflare Turnstile (already in the stack: `src/lib/turnstile.ts`): `[auth.captcha] enabled = true, provider = "turnstile", secret = "env(...)"` locally and the same switch on the hosted project (add it to I28), render the Turnstile widget on the sign-in form and pass `options: { captchaToken }` to signInWithOtp. Record the residual (a solver-backed attacker) in docs/operations.md.
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted project only (never 127.0.0.1:54320-54329): `for i in $(seq 1 31); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/otp" -H "apikey: $PUBLISHABLE_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"<a staff address>","create_user":false}'; sleep 61; done` answers 200 each time with no captcha (wrong result: 200 without a token); after the 30th mail in the hour, a sign-in from the admin page for any other staff address answers 429 over_email_send_rate_limit; the Resend dashboard shows each code counted against the day's 100.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 X-SEC-1 (marked refuted by both verification runs, no reason recorded; re-proved here from current vendor sources); lead:CLIENT-SEC-01

findings.title: The staff sign-in code is 6 digits and Supabase throttles wrong guesses only per IP, with no per-account lockout: a staff session can be brute-forced
findings.evidence: `otp_length = 6`, `otp_expiry = 600` (config.toml:240-242; I28 sets the hosted project the same). GoTrue's POST /verify carries only `limitHandler(api.limiterOpts.Verify)` (internal/api/api.go:270) and verifyUserAndToken compares the hashed code with no attempt counter or lockout (internal/api/verify.go:700-786, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/verify.go). Supabase's documented verification limit is 30 requests per 5 minutes per IP (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits), i.e. 8,640 guesses per IP per day. With no CAPTCHA on /otp (CLIENT-SEC-01) the attacker keeps a fresh code alive by asking for one every 10 minutes; GoTrue sends the mail inside the token transaction (magic_link.go:138-142), so issuance stops only when Resend refuses mail.
findings.impact: Each attacking IP has about 60 guesses per 10-minute code out of 10^6: roughly 0.6-0.9% per day per IP (≈100-144 codes a day), about 50% per day with 100 rotating IPs, and the staff-address oracle (CLIENT-SEC-02) gives the targets. A won guess is a full aal1 session for that member: for the owner or operations, every customer's and order's name, email, phone and address (customers_read_staff, the orders_list and order_detail RPCs); for the owner, prices, coupons, shipping and published content too (only refunds, recorded disputes, team changes, the seller settings, policy approval and the checkout switch need the TOTP step-up: supabase/functions/_shared/admin.ts:223-249, staff-admin/index.ts:52). Against an owner who has not enrolled TOTP yet (the bootstrap owner before his first step-up, or a newly invited owner), the won session can enrol the attacker's own factor in «الأمان» and then pass every step-up too, refunds included (the path AUDIT-2 X-SEC-2 described; GoTrue only refuses aal1 enrolment once a verified factor exists). The owner's inbox receives each code but he has no way to stop the attempts.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise the email code to 8 digits (Supabase allows 6-10): `otp_length = 8` in supabase/config.toml and in I28's hosted checklist, give `otpDigits` a length parameter (8 for the sign-in code, 6 for TOTP; src/lib/digits.ts:2) and change «رمزًا من 6 أرقام» in SignIn.tsx:12. Together with Auth CAPTCHA on /otp (CLIENT-SEC-01) this cuts the per-IP success rate about a hundredfold; 10 digits removes it in practice.
findings.proof_recipe: On a disposable stack the orchestrator owns (never 127.0.0.1:54320-54329 here) or the hosted project with a test staff user: request a code, then send 30 wrong `POST /auth/v1/verify {type:'email', email, token:'000000'..}` from one address: each answers 403 otp_expired and the 31st 429 over_request_rate_limit. Then verify the real code from a second source address (or after 5 minutes): it answers 200 with a session (wrong result: no lockout after 30 failures, so guessing continues from any other IP).
findings.prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1, AUDIT-2 and ISSUES never discuss the code length or verify throttling)

findings.title: The sign-in page hides whether an address is staff, but the Auth API it calls answers 422 otp_disabled for every non-staff address
findings.evidence: The masking is browser-only: `if (sendError?.status === 429) ... setMessage(SENT_MESSAGE)` turns every other error into «إن كان هذا البريد مسجّلًا لدينا…». GoTrue's OTP handler (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/otp.go) answers an unknown address with create_user=false by `NewUnprocessableEntityError(ErrorCodeOTPDisabled, "Signups not allowed for otp")` (HTTP 422) and a staff address with 200. tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts:9 'an unknown email gets the identical sent message' checks only the page text, while WORK-PACKAGES P03's proof says 'an unknown email gets the same response as a staff email'.
findings.impact: Anyone with the publishable key (in every page) can confirm which addresses are Anas's and his team's sign-in addresses, one request each (30 per 5 minutes per IP, and only one OTP per 60 s per real address). That gives an attacker the exact targets for code phishing, for CLIENT-SEC-01's mail flood and for CLIENT-SEC-06's guessing; the plan believes the opposite.
findings.proposed_fix: Enabling Auth CAPTCHA (CLIENT-SEC-01) throttles the oracle; to remove it, request the code through a small Edge Function that verifies Turnstile and always answers 200, calling GoTrue server-side. At minimum correct the P03 proof wording and docs to say the page, not the API, masks the address, and record the residual.
findings.proof_recipe: Hosted project only: `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST "$SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/otp" -H "apikey: $PUBLISHABLE_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nobody-<random>@example.com","create_user":false}'` prints {"code":422,"error_code":"otp_disabled",...} 422, while the same call for a staff address prints {} 200 (the wrong result the plan rules out: two different answers).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-02 (rated low there); the P03 proof claim and tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts:9 cover only the page text

findings.evidence: registerAllowlistTransforms only rewrites HeadingNode, LinkNode and TabNode. findings.title: The admin's Supabase client keeps the implicit flow with URL session detection: any link to /admin carrying another account's tokens replaces the signed-in session
findings.evidence: `client = createClient(url, key)` keeps auth-js defaults `detectSessionInUrl: true, flowType: 'implicit'` (node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.117.1/node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/module/GoTrueClient.js:14-21). `_initialize` (lines 383-421) treats any URL whose query or fragment has access_token as a callback, checks the token with `_getUser`, then `_saveSession` overwrites the stored session and emits SIGNED_IN; parseParametersFromURL reads both `?` and `#`. SignIn.tsx:73 also plans Google sign-in through this implicit redirect to `/admin`.
findings.impact: A staff member (the only people with sessions) sends the owner a link such as /admin#access_token=<own token>&refresh_token=…&expires_in=3600&token_type=bearer: the owner's tab becomes that member's session (login CSRF; the only sign is a shorter menu), so what he then types, saves or uploads is attributed to and limited by the other account until he notices. Once Google sign-in is switched on, the real access and refresh tokens arrive in the /admin URL and the fragment is cleared by assigning location.hash, which leaves the token URL in the tab's history.
findings.proposed_fix: `createClient(url, key, { auth: { flowType: 'pkce' } })`: a PKCE callback is honoured only when this browser holds the matching code verifier, so an injected link is ignored, and Google returns a one-time ?code= instead of tokens. (While Google stays off, `detectSessionInUrl: false` is the one-line alternative.)
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: The site's baseline headers carry no Strict-Transport-Security (the soon page does), so moving anas.studio to the Pages project drops HSTS; COOP and Permissions-Policy are also absent
findings.evidence: The `/*` block sends only X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and a CSP; no Strict-Transport-Security, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy or Permissions-Policy anywhere in the file. The live soon site sends `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` from artifacts/soon/site/_headers:10 (MAINT-1 fix). Cloudflare does not add HSTS by default: it is the zone's opt-in Edge Certificates setting or a header the site sends (https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/http-strict-transport-security/; default Pages headers: https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/serving-pages/). PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md's header list and the P11 hosted checklist (I28, I32) do not mention HSTS. Chromium's preload list (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/net/http/transport_security_state_static.json, read 2026-10-07) holds TLD entries for "app" and "dev" but none for "studio" or "anas.studio", so only a header protects the domain.
findings.impact: A browser keeps an HSTS policy it already has, so the soon page's visitors stay covered for a year; every visitor who first arrives after the P11 switch never receives one, and each of their plain-HTTP entries (a typed anas.studio, an old http:// link) goes out unprotected, so a hostile network can strip the Always-Use-HTTPS redirect and serve a look-alike /admin/sign-in or checkout page that captures the emailed code or a TOTP. Without COOP, a cross-origin page that opened the admin with window.open keeps a handle to navigate that tab (tab-nabbing).
findings.proposed_fix: Add to the `/*` block of public/_headers: `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` (the soon page's value, so nothing changes at the switch), `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()`; add HSTS to the DATA-AND-SECURITY header list and to tests/e2e/security.spec.ts with the P10 CSP.
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted Pages preview after P10/P11: `curl -sI https://<preview or anas.studio>/ | grep -i strict-transport` prints nothing today (wrong result); after the fix it prints max-age=31536000.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-06; I46 covers only the full CSP; MAINT-1 added HSTS to the soon site only

findings.title: The rich-text link rule accepts HTTPS:// and https:host spellings that the public renderer then draws as plain text
findings.evidence: The editor and the publish/build schema use `httpsUrl = z.url({ protocol: /^https$/ })` (src/admin/richtext.ts:25), which compares the parsed protocol and, because the regex is not zod's http one, skips the '://' guard (zod 4.6.5 parseURLObject). The renderer keeps a link only when `node.url.startsWith('https://')`. Measured with zod 4.6.5 (scratch url-check.mjs): 'HTTPS://example.com', 'https:example.com' and 'https:/example.com' are all accepted by the schema and all render without a link.
findings.impact: A link Anas pastes or types with an upper-case scheme (common from Word or a phone keyboard) or without the slashes shows as a link in the editor and passes publishing, then silently loses its link on the public page and in the preview; nothing tells him why.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the stored value canonical where it is validated: `z.url({ protocol: /^https$/, normalize: true })` in src/admin/richtext.ts (the build and the preview render the parsed, normalized `https://…/` form), or have the renderer use the same rule (`httpsUrl.safeParse(url)` and its output) instead of `startsWith`.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-05; AUDIT-2 ADMIN-publish-2 (contested; the opposite mismatch, editor looser than the schema, which the httpsUrl change fixed)

findings.title: The store build accepts any string as a product cover, so a `media|https://other.host/…` value becomes an from a foreign origin on /store
findings.evidence: `cover_image: z.string().nullable()` (store.ts:29) with no id rule, then `replaceMediaIds(row.cover_image, …)` (store.ts:126) and `<Picture id={product.cover}>` (src/app/(public)/store/page.tsx:46-48, [slug]/page.tsx:75-77) → imageSources → parseMediaRef accepts `media|<any base>|WxH|widths` (src/lib/media-ref.ts:77-97) and emits `src="<base>/<w>.webp"`. The column only checks length (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:120 `char_length(cover_image) between 1 and 120`); the admin form's image rule (src/admin/fields.ts:266-268) runs in the browser only, while every content image is re-checked by the collection schema at build.
findings.impact: Only an owner session can write products (products_update_owner), so visitors and editors cannot use it; but an owner token used directly against the Data API (a stolen session, CLIENT-SEC-06, or a bad import) can put a tracking or replacement image from any host on the store and product pages, which the content path would refuse at build.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate the column in productRowSchema with the content rule: `cover_image: z.string().refine((id) => Object.hasOwn(imageManifest, id) || isMediaId(id)).nullable()` (reuse the image id schema from src/admin/fields.ts), so the build fails like a bad room document.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-08

findings.title: Password recovery stays a sign-in-by-link path: /recover is anonymous, the template is Supabase's English default with a login link, and the hook lets 'recovery' through
findings.evidence: deny_password_tokens refuses only `authentication_method = 'password'`; its own comment (lines 14-19) passes 'recovery' through. supabase/config.toml:254-262 customises only `[auth.email.template.magic_link]` (code only); recovery has no template here and I28 names only the magic-link one. GoTrue registers POST /recover with only the per-IP limiter and verifyCaptcha (internal/api/api.go), and the recovery mail's link verifies type=recovery and returns a session.
findings.impact: Anyone can make the studio's sender mail Anas (or any staff address) an English 'Reset Password' message whose link signs the holder in at aal1, once per 60 s per address and without CAPTCHA: a second, link-based way in that D08's code-only design removed from the magic-link mail (a forwarded or previewed mail carries a live login), a ready pretext for phishing in a language the product never uses, and more spend on the shared Resend quota (CLIENT-SEC-01).
findings.proposed_fix: Add `[auth.email.template.recovery]` with an Arabic body that carries no link or token («لا تُستخدم كلمات مرور في لوحة أنس؛ تجاهل هذه الرسالة.»), apply it on the hosted project (I28), and refuse `authentication_method = 'recovery'` in deny_password_tokens as it refuses 'password' (staff have no passwords to recover).
findings.proof_recipe: On a disposable stack: `curl -X POST $SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/recover -H "apikey: $PUBLISHABLE_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"<staff>"}'` answers 200 with no captcha; the mail (Mailpit) is the English default with a /auth/v1/verify?…&type=recovery link; opening it returns 303 with #access_token=… (wrong result: a session from a link, not from the code).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-03; AUDIT-1 S01.4 (password half only)

findings.title: «تسجيل الخروج» ignores a failed signOut: when the stored token has expired and the network is down, the session stays in localStorage while the page shows the sign-in screen
findings.evidence: AdminShell.signOut: `clearDrafts(); await getSupabaseBrowserClient().auth.signOut(); router.replace('/admin/sign-in')`, result never read. auth-js 2.117.1: `_signOut` returns `{ error: sessionError }` before `removeCurrentSession()` when the session read fails (GoTrueClient.js:3424-3433); `__loadSession` fails that way when the access token is past expiry and the refresh errors (lines 2541-2569), and `_callRefreshToken` keeps the stored session on a retryable fetch error (lines 4292-4313).
findings.impact: The owner wakes a laptop after more than an hour, presses «تسجيل الخروج» before the Wi-Fi is back, sees the sign-in page and walks away from a shared or borrowed computer; the refresh token is still stored and still valid (Supabase sessions do not expire by default), so the next person who opens /admin is signed in as him, with customers' data and prices in reach.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the result and do not pretend: `const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut(); if (error) { setSignOutError('تعذّر تسجيل الخروج؛ تحقق من الاتصال ثم حاول مرة أخرى.'); return }` and redirect only after a successful call. (`signOut({ scope: 'local' })` is no fallback: `_signOut` returns the session-read error before it looks at the scope, GoTrueClient.js:3430-3433.)
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-04; AUDIT-2 ADMIN-editor-3 (drafts half)

findings.title: A 5xx from Supabase Auth (the SMTP send failed) is shown as «أرسلنا إليه رمزًا» and the page moves to the code step
findings.evidence: SignIn.tsx:43-52 maps only a status-less error to OFFLINE_MESSAGE and 429 to RATE_LIMITED_MESSAGE; everything else, including 500, reaches `setMessage(SENT_MESSAGE); setStep('code')`. GoTrue answers a failed mail send with `NewInternalServerError("Error sending magic link email")` and keeps the old token (internal/api/mail.go:497-510).
findings.impact: While Resend refuses mail (the daily quota spent, CLIENT-SEC-01, or an SMTP outage) every staff member is told a code was sent, waits for a mail that never comes, and retries into the same sentence; nothing on the page says that mail is down.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat `sendError.status >= 500` like the network case with its own sentence («تعذّر إرسال الرمز الآن؛ حاول بعد قليل.») and stay on the email step; keep the masked answer for 2xx and 4xx only (a 5xx reveals nothing about the address).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:CLIENT-SEC-10; AUDIT-2 ADMIN-auth-8 (fixed the network half)

findings.title: The /book page's JavaScript ships the whole book-source manifest, including the owner's internal approval note and the source file inventory
findings.evidence: `import manifest from '../../content/book-source-manifest.json'` in a module the client reader uses; only `manifest.output.url` and `manifest.pages` are read, but the bundler keeps the whole object. out/_next/static/chunks/2667kept7dvnv.js and 2uzaovfm1pqub.js (both referenced by out/book.html and out/book.txt) contain `approval:{by:"owner",date:"2026-09-28",words:"ANAS provide two or three PDF texts !! we only want to let users see these then had to buy the whole book to read"}`, `tool:"pypdf 6.16.2"` and `inputs:[{file:"BOOK_ASSETS/ (8).pdf",sha256:…,bytes:…}, …]`.

findings.title: check:export does not scan .mjs (or .svg) files, so the secret and demo scans miss part of out/
findings.evidence: `const TEXT = /\.(html|txt|js|css|json|map|xml|webmanifest)$|[\\/]_headers$/`; the export holds out/_next/static/media/pdf.worker.min.*.mjs and four .svg files that are never read. The header comment says 'no file contains a server-side secret'.

findings.title: Every Edge Function reaches the database only through the legacy service_role key, which new or restored Supabase projects no longer have
findings.evidence: db.ts:30 `admin ??= createClient(requireEnv("SUPABASE_URL"), requireEnv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"), {` is the only service client (staff.ts getClaims + staff lookup, admin.ts rpc/storage, staff-admin, outbox, resend-webhook all go through it); repo-wide grep finds no reader of SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS (only db.ts:30 and two integration tests). Supabase (https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/29260, fetched 2026-10-07): "Projects restored from 1st November 2025 will no longer be restored with the legacy API keys. New projects no longer have anon and service_role available for use" and "Late 2026, TBC: Legacy API keys will be deleted"; https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys.md: "deprecating the anon and service_role keys by the end of 2026"; https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/secrets.md lists SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY under "Legacy keys" and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS (JSON) as the default secret.
findings.impact: The plan runs ONE free hosted project (DECISIONS build policy). A project created after 2025-11-01, or the free project restored after an inactivity pause, has no legacy service_role key; at the latest the keys are deleted in late 2026, around launch. Then serviceClient() has no usable key: every admin/staff-admin call answers 500 (staff lookup throws), the outbox sends nothing (receipts, notices), the Resend webhook answers 503 to every event until Svix disables the endpoint, and checkout/payments fail the same way. PLANS/ARCHITECTURE.md:109 says only "The service-role key is provided to the functions by Supabase"; no package schedules the switch.
findings.proposed_fix: In serviceClient() take the key from JSON.parse(SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS).default when present, falling back to SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; add "functions use the sb_secret key; legacy keys disabled" to the P11 hosted checklist (I28) and prove one function against the hosted project.
findings.proof_recipe: On the hosted project: Dashboard > Settings > API Keys shows whether legacy keys exist/are enabled. With legacy keys disabled (or absent), call POST <functions_url>/admin {action:"status"} with an owner JWT: wrong result is 500 FAILED (staff lookup throws) instead of 200.
findings.prior_overlap: none found in AUDIT-1/AUDIT-2/ISSUES

findings.title: Revoking a staff member never ends their sessions, so a later restore revives every old session on every device
findings.evidence: set_active(false) only flips staff.active and bans: `(await admin.auth.admin.updateUserById(userId, { ban_duration: BAN_FOREVER })).error` (line 134); set_active(true) lifts it: `updateUserById(userId, { ban_duration: 'none' })` (line 126). Nothing deletes auth.sessions/refresh_tokens (grep: only privacy_erase_staff, 20260927140000_privacy_requests.sql:87-92). Supabase Auth source (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/tokens/service.go, refresh grant): `if user.IsBanned() { return ... "Invalid Refresh Token: User Banned") }`, then the session is checked only for existence/timebox; the admin.go ban path calls only `user.Ban(tx, *banDuration)` (no Logout). A ban suspends refresh; the unban makes the same refresh tokens valid again.
findings.impact: A member is revoked because a laptop was lost or they left, then later restored (new device, rehire, a mistaken revoke undone). Every browser signed in before the revoke silently refreshes and regains staff access (an owner session regains owner rights, its aal2 kept) with no new email code. DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:99 promises the opposite: 'Removing a staff member sets active=false and signs out their sessions.'
findings.proposed_fix: On revoke, delete the member's sessions right after the ban through a service_role-only SQL function (`delete from auth.sessions where user_id = p_user`, as privacy_erase_staff already does), answering like BAN_FAILED when it fails.
findings.proof_recipe: Local stack: sign in as an editor in browser A; owner revokes, then restores the editor through staff-admin; in browser A run supabase.auth.refreshSession(). Wrong result: a new session is returned, and `select count(*) from auth.sessions where user_id = '<editor>'` was > 0 right after the revoke.
findings.prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1 S07.7 covered only the ban-lift error message)

findings.title: An account-level Resend refusal (revoked key, unverified domain) exhausts every queued mail on its first attempt instead of pausing the outbox
findings.evidence: classifyResendFailure: `if (status >= 500) return { outcome: 'retry', ... }` then `return { outcome: 'permanent', error: `HTTP_${status}` }` (email.ts:74-75) for every other 4xx, including 401/403 (the comment at line 60 lists '403 unverified domain or suspended key'). outbox_result turns a permanent outcome into status 'exhausted' at once (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:597-604), and runOutbox keeps claiming the next row (it stops early only on QUOTA, outbox.ts:281), up to 10 rows per minute while rows are due. Resend's errors page (https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/errors.md, 2026-10-07): missing_api_key 401, restricted_api_key 403 'API key is not active', suspended_api_key 403, validation_error 403 'The `domain.com` domain is not verified' and 'You can only send testing emails to your own email address'; all are about the account, not the message.
findings.impact: If the API key is rotated without updating the secret, the sending domain's DNS verification lapses, or the domain is still unverified at launch, every receipt, order link, notice and owner alert is marked exhausted within minutes of being queued; nothing is retried when the key or domain is fixed, and the owner must replay each row by hand from البريد (the list shows at most 200 rows; past 23 h each replay needs the duplicate-risk confirmation).
findings.proposed_fix: Classify 401 and 403 like QUOTA: a retry with a distinct code (e.g. PROVIDER_CONFIG) that gives the attempt back, defers the row (e.g. 15 minutes) and stops the run, and record the run as failed with that reason so the owner home shows it.
findings.prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-1 S04.2 fixed the QUOTA case only)

findings.title: admin buffers the whole request body before its 16 KiB check, and any genuine staff JWT (a revoked member's included) reaches that read
findings.evidence: admin.ts:191-194: `if (!staff) return fail(401, ...)` then `const text = await request.text()` then `if (new TextEncoder().encode(text).length > MAX_BODY_BYTES) return fail(413, ...)`. staffFromRequest returns `{ userId, role: null, ... }` for a valid token whose staff row is inactive (staff.ts:47), so it passes the 401 gate; the role checks run only in the switch after the read. `boundedText` (http.ts:54-71), which refuses a declared content-length and cancels the stream at the limit, exists and is used by resend-webhook.ts:111 but not here.
findings.impact: Any holder of a valid staff access token (editor, operations, or a revoked member whose JWT has not expired when the project uses asymmetric JWT keys, i.e. getClaims verifies locally) can make the admin isolate buffer an arbitrarily large body before it is refused (platform memory 256 MB, https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/limits). Availability of the admin function only; no data effect. staff-admin/index.ts:59-60 has the same read-then-check but only a stepped-up owner reaches it.
findings.proposed_fix: Read with `const text = await boundedText(request, MAX_BODY_BYTES); if (text === null) return fail(413, ...)`, and return 403 for `staff.role === null` before reading the body.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-01 (and lead:EF-ADMIN-02 for staff-admin, folded in)

findings.title: paid-file-complete replaces the file every future buyer downloads at aal1: no TOTP step-up
findings.evidence: admin.ts:250-255: `case 'paid-file-ticket': if (staff.role !== 'owner') return fail(403, ...)` / `case 'paid-file-complete': if (staff.role !== 'owner') return fail(403, ...); return paidFileComplete(...)` with no `if (!staff.recentTotp)` line, unlike refund-create, dispute-record and the three commerce actions. paid-files.ts:3-4 states the choice: 'no fresh TOTP: nothing here moves money'. The server checks only the head (`%PDF-`, or an EPUB's first ZIP entry, paid-files.ts:128-143); paid_asset_set hands the new object to waiting entitlements and to every later order (P08-CONTRACT section 7).
findings.impact: Precondition: an owner session at aal1 (an emailed code obtained by someone with access to the owner's mailbox, a stolen token, an unlocked device). The holder can swap the paid e-book for any file that begins with `%PDF-`; every later buyer downloads it under Anas's name and the ledger shows an ordinary owner action. TOTP guards money and team changes but not the product delivered for money.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the same `if (!staff.recentTotp) return fail(403, 'STEP_UP_REQUIRED', ...)` to paid-file-complete (VariantCommerce can reuse withStepUp), or record the owner's explicit acceptance of the aal1 risk in P08-CONTRACT section 7.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-03; P08-CONTRACT section 7 documents 'owner' without TOTP

findings.title: The media upload ticket expires 5 minutes after creation, so a large upload over a slow uplink can never complete
findings.evidence: `expires_at timestamptz not null default now() + interval '5 minutes'` (media_library.sql:107); media_claim raises object_not_in_prerequisite_state when `t.expires_at <= now()` (line 253), mapped to 410 GONE «انتهت صلاحية التذكرة أو استُخدمت من قبل.» (media.ts:125-126). MediaUpload.tsx:252-269 asks for the ticket, then uploads the original (up to 15 MiB) and up to four derivatives (up to 4 MiB each) one after another, and only then calls media-complete; «إعادة المحاولة» repeats the same sequence with a new ticket.
findings.impact: An editor (or Anas) on an uplink under roughly 0.5 Mbit/s uploads every byte of a 15 MiB photo, then is told the ticket expired or was used, and every retry fails the same way; the parts sit in quarantine until the daily sweep. Large uploads are impossible from such a connection.
findings.proposed_fix: Let the signed URLs bound the upload time and raise the ticket expiry (e.g. 30 minutes), which still caps open tickets at 10 per actor.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-04

findings.title: An AVIF whose ftyp major brand is not literally 'avif' (for example 'mif1') is refused as UNKNOWN_TYPE
findings.evidence: media.ts:179 `const mime = measured.type ? DETECTED_MIME[measured.type] : undefined` with DETECTED_MIME = {jpg, png, webp, avif}. image-size 2.0.4 (node_modules/image-size/dist/esm/types/heif.js:2-10,19-20,29,63): validate() accepts major brands avif, mif1, msf1, heic, heix, hevc, hevx, and calculate() returns `type: toUTF8String(input, 8, 12)`, the raw major brand. A valid AVIF still image written with major brand 'mif1' (compatible brand 'avif') yields type 'mif1'; an AVIF sequence ('avis') is not even validated.
findings.impact: The browser decodes the file (createImageBitmap), MediaUpload declares image/avif, every part uploads, then media-complete answers 422 «لم يُعرف نوع الملف من محتواه أو أنه نوع غير مسموح.» with no hint; bounded to one input type (re-exporting as JPEG or WebP works).
findings.proposed_fix: Accept 'mif1'/'msf1' as image/avif when the ftyp box lists 'avif' among its compatible brands (a few lines over the head bytes already read).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-05; distinct from I49(2) (rotation)

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md says Supabase Auth mail follows the outbox's suppression and quota policy; it follows neither
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:99: 'All outbound mail, including Supabase Auth mail through SMTP, follows the same suppression and quota policy.' Sign-in codes go out through GoTrue's SMTP connection (I28) and never pass outbox_claim, the only reader of finance.email_suppressions and the only place the day's sends are counted (20261002120000_order_emails.sql:277-312). docs/operations.md:270-279 itself says the codes 'share the account but are not counted (residual risk)'.
findings.impact: An operator reasoning from the plan of record expects a suppressed address to stop receiving sign-in codes and the reserve arithmetic to include auth mail; neither holds, so reserve sizing and incident handling built on that sentence are wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the sentence with what is true: Auth mail shares the Resend account's quota and Resend's own suppression list, but not finance.email_suppressions or the outbox counts (as docs/operations.md:270-279 says).
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-06

findings.title: One permanent bounce of the owner's address silently suppresses every later owner alert and contact notice, and no runbook says how to lift it
findings.evidence: operations.md:300-301: 'Re-allowing a recipient is a deliberate manual database action, not an automatic one.' No migration, function or doc deletes from finance.email_suppressions (grep: inserts and selects only), the key is finance.recipient_hash(lower(btrim(email))) (20260926120000_contacts_and_email.sql:145-152), and the reason 'manual' is never written. email_event_record inserts a suppression for any email.bounced whose type is not temporary/soft/transient (20260930140000_audit2_fixes.sql:646-658), for any mail Resend reports for the account; outbox_claim then marks every pending owner_alert and contact_notice for that address 'suppressed' (20261002120000_order_emails.sql:277-283), and outbox_replay refuses them (check_violation).
findings.impact: After one hard bounce at the owner's address (a mailbox migration, a provider hiccup classed Permanent), payment_review, needs_resolution, external_refund and contact notices stop arriving with no mail error anywhere; the attention list shows «محظور» rows and offers nothing, and the cure is SQL the runbook does not give.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to docs/operations.md the exact statement `delete from finance.email_suppressions where recipient_hash = finance.recipient_hash('<address>');` plus a step to replay the held rows, and say that a staff address can be the one suppressed.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-07

findings.title: The settings status calls the Resend webhook configured for any non-empty secret, so a mis-pasted secret fails every delivery event silently
findings.evidence: admin.ts:622 `webhook: optionalEnv('RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET') !== undefined`. verifySvixSignature strips an optional `whsec_` and base64-decodes the rest (email.ts:643-649); a value that does not decode, or a wrong secret, makes every signed delivery answer 401 (resend-webhook.ts:134-136). No job run, counter or screen records webhook receipt; a sent row whose events never arrive keeps delivery null, which operations.md:325-326 describes as the normal state.
findings.impact: At P11 a secret pasted with a missing character passes the status check (SettingsView shows مضبوط), Svix retries and eventually disables the endpoint, and no bounce or complaint is ever recorded: suppression stops working while everything looks healthy.
findings.proposed_fix: Report `webhook` as configured only when the secret has the whsec_ form and decodes to a non-empty key, and record the time of the last verified event (one row or a job_run) so the owner home can show when events stop.
findings.prior_overlap: lead:EF-ADMIN-08

findings.title: The contact notice keeps the visitor's own bidi controls, so a name or message line can close its isolate and reverse the rest of the line

The order mails use one() (email.ts:334-341), which drops \p{Bidi_Control}. contact.ts:71 and :80 accept any characters (`z.string().trim().min(1).max(120)` / `.max(5000)`). A Node run of the repo's renderContactNotice with the name 'Ali U+2069 U+202E moc.liamg@sana' (scratch bidi-check.mjs) printed `الاسم: U+2068 Ali U+2069 U+202E moc.liamg@sana U+2069`, while renderOrderLink with the same name printed it with both controls removed.

findings.title: A row that turns 'pending' after an uncertain attempt escapes the 23-hour idempotency window and can be resent blindly days later
findings.evidence: outbox_result sets `status = 'pending'` on any non-QUOTA retry (line 593) and on a QUOTA give-back when the next UTC midnight is within 23 h of first_attempt_at (lines 570-572), even when an earlier attempt of the row was 'uncertain'. outbox_claim applies the window only to uncertain rows: `o.status = 'pending' or (o.status = 'uncertain' and o.first_attempt_at > now() - interval '23 hours')` (20261002120000_order_emails.sql:320-321), and a pending row can wait past midnight for days behind the tier caps (`v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - ...`). Resend keeps a key 24 hours (https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/emails/idempotency-keys).
findings.impact: Example: attempt 1 of an availability or receipt mail times out after Resend accepted it (uncertain); attempt 2 meets a 5xx or the daily quota and the row becomes pending; its tier stays full for more than a day; the claim then sends it again with an expired key and the buyer gets a duplicate. operations.md and outbox_due_since promise that a possibly-delivered row past 23 h waits for a person's replay.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the row 'uncertain' instead of 'pending' once any earlier attempt was uncertain (a flag set by the uncertain branch), so the claim's 23-hour guard applies.
findings.proof_recipe: Local DB as service_role: insert a finance.email_outbox row (kind 'receipt', priority 0); `select * from outbox_claim(1,120,100,20,3000,30)`; `select outbox_result(<id>,<lease>,'uncertain',null,'NETWORK')`; `update finance.email_outbox set next_at=now() where id=<id>`; claim again; `select outbox_result(<id>,<lease2>,'retry',null,'HTTP_503')` gives status 'pending'; `update finance.email_outbox set first_attempt_at=now()-interval '30 hours', next_at=now() where id=<id>`; claim again. Wrong result: the row is claimed ('sending') although its first, possibly delivered attempt is 30 h old.
findings.prior_overlap: related to AUDIT-2 DB-auditfix-3 (the opposite case, fixed)

findings.title: After BAN_FAILED the screen says «حاول مرة أخرى», but the only button left on the row restores the member
findings.evidence: set_active(false) commits `active = false` (index.ts:129-131), then the ban fails and the reply is `fail(500, 'BAN_FAILED', 'حُدّثت الحالة لكن تعذّر إيقاف الدخول. حاول مرة أخرى.')` (line 136). TeamView.runAction shows that message and reloads (TeamView.tsx:93-96); the reloaded row is inactive, so its button is «استعادة» (TeamView.tsx:214-225: `runAction({ action: 'set_active', userId, active: !member.active })`), which unbans and re-activates (index.ts:125-131). The function would re-apply the ban for an already inactive member (set_active false again), but the screen offers no control for it, and staff_directory exposes no ban state.
findings.impact: An owner revoking a member during an Auth admin hiccup follows «حاول مرة أخرى» with the row's only button and restores the person they meant to remove (no confirmation is asked for a restore). If they do not, the member stays unbanned: they can still sign in (no data access while inactive), and EF-ADMIN-02 keeps their sessions.
findings.proposed_fix: Word BAN_FAILED as «أُوقف العضو، لكن تعذّر منع دخوله؛ أعد الإيقاف بعد قليل» and let the screen offer «إيقاف» again for that row (re-sending set_active false), e.g. by returning {active:false, banned:false} and keeping it in state.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S07.7 fixed the restore direction's message only

findings.title: media-complete deletes the image's objects when the media_complete call's outcome is unknown, so a committed row can point at nothing
findings.evidence: admin.ts:392-397: `try { await rpc('media_complete', {...}) } catch (error) { await cleanupAll(); return sqlFail(error) }`. cleanupAll removes the public derivatives and the moved original (admin.ts:325-327). A network failure or a lost reply reaches here as a DbError with code '' (postgrest-js 2.117.1 dist/index.cjs:418-455 maps any fetchError to `code: ""`; RPC POSTs are never retried, RETRYABLE_METHODS = GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, lines 83-87), the same as a refusal. paid-files.ts:291-296 makes exactly this distinction ('A call whose outcome is unknown ... may have been committed') and keeps the object; media-complete does not.
findings.impact: When the reply to a committed media_complete is lost, the editor is told «تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.» and retries (a new ticket, a second row), while the first media row stays in the library with its original and every derivative deleted: a broken entry that can be picked into a document or a product cover, whose public image then 404s.
findings.proposed_fix: Clean up only when the error carries a SQLSTATE outside class 08 (the SQLSTATE test paid-files.ts already uses); on an unknown outcome keep the objects and answer 500 so the row, if committed, stays whole.
findings.prior_overlap: none (I34 covers leftovers after a delete, not this)

findings.title: The step-up dialog says «الرمز غير صحيح.» for every failure, a lost connection or Auth's MFA rate limit included
findings.evidence: StepUp.tsx:43-47: `const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challengeAndVerify({ factorId, code })` then `if (verifyError) { setError('الرمز غير صحيح.'); return }`, whatever the error (no status check). MfaEnroll.tsx:79-81 does the same. SignIn.tsx:43-50 already tells an offline request (`!sendError.status`) and a 429 apart. Supabase limits MFA challenge/verify to 15 per minute per IP (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits.md).
findings.impact: An owner confirming a refund or a team change on a flaky connection, or after a few quick tries, is told the code is wrong, types fresh codes into a request that cannot succeed and keeps spending the per-minute MFA budget; the money or team action seems blocked by a bad authenticator.
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror SignIn: no status means «تعذّر الاتصال…», status 429 means «محاولات كثيرة؛ انتظر دقيقة», anything else stays «الرمز غير صحيح.».
findings.prior_overlap: none

findings.title: The owner home never shows the payments_reconcile job, so a failed or stalled reconciliation raises no signal
findings.evidence: AdminHome.tsx:33 `const KNOWN_JOBS = ['email_outbox', 'site_build', 'media_sweep', 'backup'] as const` and JOB_LABEL (lines 25-30) have no payments_reconcile, although jobs.ts:23-48 and :79-81 record it (`job_run_record('payments_reconcile', ...)`, 'skipped' while payments are not configured) and job_runs_latest returns every job. payments_kick (20261002100000_payment_core.sql:1643-1675) calls the job only while an attempt, an event or a refund is due, and nothing like outbox_due_since exists for it, so neither a recorded 'failed' run nor a job that stopped being called reaches any screen.
findings.impact: The reconciliation is the backstop for a missed Moyasar webhook, an uncertain invoice creation and a refund in flight. If it fails every run (a bug, a provider outage) or stops being called (Vault value missing after a restore, a JOBS_SECRET mismatch), paid orders whose webhook was lost stay unsettled and attempts never turn UNVERIFIED, so «تحتاج مطابقة» stays low; the owner learns of it from buyers. Latent until checkout opens.
findings.proposed_fix: Add payments_reconcile to KNOWN_JOBS and JOB_LABEL (reading a 'skipped' run's detail.reason as 'payments not configured'), and warn when work has been due longer than a few minutes, from a payments_due_since like outbox_due_since.
findings.prior_overlap: listed in P08 round-12b 'Uncovered' (not ruled, not in ISSUES I51)

findings.title: Storage and Auth calls through supabase-js in admin/staff carry no timeout; only the platform's 150 s limit ends a hung media-complete

plan_gaps.title: Move the Edge Functions off the legacy service_role key and prove it on the hosted project
plan_gaps.why_needed: db.ts reads only SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; Supabase's new and restored projects have no legacy keys (discussion 29260) and the keys are deprecated by the end of 2026, so the first hosted deploy, or the free project's first restore after a pause, can leave every function without database access (EF-ADMIN-01). No package or checklist item names it.
plan_gaps.touches: supabase/functions/_shared/db.ts; PLANS/ISSUES.md I28 (hosted checklist); docs/deployment.md
plan_gaps.package: P11 (the code change can land in P08's next round)

plan_gaps.title: Decide the mail plan for launch day: Resend's 100/day is shared by receipts and staff sign-in codes, and priority 0 may use all of it
plan_gaps.why_needed: outbox_claim lets priority 0 (receipts, order mail, owner alerts) send while the day's outbox sends are under 100 (P08-CONTRACT section 8), and Supabase Auth's codes on the same Resend account are not counted at all. On a day with roughly 80-100+ orders the receipts use the whole quota: the rest wait for the next UTC day and every staff sign-in code fails until midnight, so the owner cannot enter the admin on the busiest day. outbox.ts:46-54 and operations.md:172-173 say the reserve stays free for sign-in codes, docs/costs.md:13 says it is for receipts; neither is guaranteed. costs.md:23 lists Resend Pro only as a cost trigger, not as a precondition of opening checkout.
plan_gaps.touches: docs/costs.md; PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md section 8; supabase/functions/_shared/outbox.ts comments; the E07 cost sheet

plan_gaps.title: A lost authenticator: no recovery procedure for the owner's TOTP factor
plan_gaps.why_needed: Every money action (refund-create, refund-record-external, dispute-record, commerce-checkout-set, settings and policy approval) and every team action needs a TOTP entry from the last five minutes. An owner who loses the phone is locked out of all of them; the only way back is deleting the factor in the Supabase dashboard (Authentication > Users), which no runbook, owner guide or P11 training item describes.
plan_gaps.touches: docs/operations.md; docs/owner-guide.ar.md; P11 training list (WORK-PACKAGES.md:141)

plan_gaps.title: A sent mail whose delivery bounced or failed cannot be re-sent
plan_gaps.why_needed: outbox_replay accepts only exhausted or uncertain rows (20261002120000_order_emails.sql:379) and EmailView offers replay only for them (EmailView.tsx:48, 238). A receipt Resend accepted and then reported as a temporary bounce or email.failed is listed under «انتهت» with no action, so the buyer never gets it unless they use the recovery form.
plan_gaps.touches: outbox_replay; src/components/admin/EmailView.tsx; docs/operations.md

plan_gaps.title: No signal that Resend delivery webhooks are arriving
plan_gaps.why_needed: Nothing records receipt of webhook events (job_runs cover the outbox, the sweep and the reconciliation only). A wrong secret, URL or a Svix-disabled endpoint leaves every sent row with delivery null, which the runbook describes as normal, so bounce suppression silently stops (see EF-ADMIN-09).
plan_gaps.touches: supabase/functions/_shared/resend-webhook.ts; AdminHome job panel; docs/operations.md

plan_gaps.title: Most owner powers run at aal1; only refunds, disputes, checkout/seller/policy settings and team changes need a fresh TOTP
plan_gaps.why_needed: An emailed sign-in code alone lets an owner session change prices, coupons and shipping (RLS owner policies), publish site content, read stats and replace the paid file buyers download (EF-ADMIN-04). The step-up list (D13, P08-CONTRACT section 7) is deliberate, but the owner has not been asked whether the deliverable and the catalog's prices should also require aal2 (Supabase can enforce aal2 in RLS for users with a verified factor).
plan_gaps.touches: PLANS/DECISIONS.md D13 note; supabase/functions/_shared/admin.ts; owner RLS policies
